samples.book: 012 - Star Wars and Philosophy - More Powerful than You Can Possibly Imagine
samples.title: “This One a Long Time Have I Watched”
samples.relation: Eberl argues that Anakin and Luke are radically free despite the Chosen One prophecy and Obi-Wan's 'you cannot escape your destiny.' Borrowing Augustine and Aquinas on God's eternity, he holds that foreknowledge (like the Jedi prophecy fulfilled when Vader destroys the Emperor) does not compel events - Anakin's choice makes the prophecy true, not vice versa - and applies Aristotle's tomorrow's-sea-battle to future-contingents like Obi-Wan's self-surrender on the Death Star. Using Locke's locked-room example and Augustine's account of 'inordinate desire,' he concludes that Anakin's fall stems from his own disordered will to control fate ('learn to stop people from dying'), while Han Solo embodies libertarian alternative possibilities ('No mystical energy field controls my destiny').

samples.book: 031 - Johnny Cash and Philosophy - The Burning Ring of Truth
samples.title: “A Boy Named Sue” A Cashian Theodicy
samples.relation: Jamie Carlin Watson reads Cash's Christian worldview as Augustinian: evil is not a positive substance but a privation or corruption of good (contra the monism Leibniz risks and the Manichean dualism Augustine rejected), so humans alone bear blame for moral evil through freely corrupting good things—'Cocaine Blues,' 'The Wall,' the Folsom prisoner who admits he 'had it coming,' and the divided self of 'The Beast in Me' echoing Romans 7. Natural evil, as in 'Guess Things Happen That Way' and the flood of 'Five Feet High and Rising' (Cash's mother's 'blessing' of rich river dirt), serves punishment or greater goods. 'A Boy Named Sue' dramatizes the residual tension: the father's get-tough-or-die theodicy convinces neither Sue nor us that the sheer amount of evil is justified.

samples.book: 067 - Breaking Bad and Philosophy - Badder Living through Chemistry
samples.title: Breaking Bad and Philosophy
samples.relation: Sets Walt's 'There's nothing but chemistry here' materialism - the missing 0.111958 percent of the human body that Gretchen calls the soul - against Augustine's Confessions, arguing both men want redemption without giving up their sins: 'give me chastity, but not yet.' It maps Augustine's problem of evil (evil as corruption of the will toward self-destruction) onto Walt's pros-and-cons list over killing Krazy-8 and his 'no-rough-stuff-type deal' fantasy after Tuco. Werner Heisenberg's uncertainty principle then turns chemistry's laws into tendencies, opening room for free choice inside a materialist world - so Walt's remission in 'Over' saves the body, while only changed choices, which he keeps deferring, could save the man.

samples.book: 190 - The Ultimate Star Wars and Philosophy - You Must Unlearn What You Have Learned
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: Eberl applies Augustine's theodicy to the Force: since evil is privation rather than a thing, the dark side is not a real half of the Force but its willful misuse by free beings, answering why a Force with a will permits Alderaan. Anakin's fall is Augustine's inordinate desire (cupiditas) for the temporal good of Padme's life against Yoda's counsel to let go, while Jacen Solo's willingness to kill for peace shows love destroyed rather than merely disordered, placing him beyond the redemption Anakin's rightly ordered love for his children still permits. Free will remains a divine gift whose misuse, not its giver, explains moral evil, and Anakin could still freely fulfill the Chosen One prophecy.

samples.book: 064 - The Rolling Stones and Philosophy - It's Just a Thought Away
samples.title: A Wild Murder Couldn’t Drag Me Away
samples.relation: Draws Augustine and Jagger together as brothers who fell far before finding restraint: Augustine's many conflicting wills must collapse into one good will by actually choosing, and his Manichean past taught him some truths must be performed or willed, like his "grant me chastity — just not yet." The chapter reads Gimme Shelter as likewise double — harrowing documentary or joyous concert footage, forced to choose — and argues the post-Altamont Stones had to make "Sympathy for the Devil" a performative force for understanding evil rather than a scapegoat, then stayed in the flesh, confronting good and evil through the blues.

samples.book: 030 - Pink Floyd and Philosophy - Careful with that Axiom, Eugene!
samples.title: We Don’t Need No Indoctrination
samples.relation: Detmer argues the four classic albums from Dark Side to The Wall form a unified meditation on alienation, from others, work, nature, and oneself, and reads Waters's stated 'political and philosophical' aims through the existentialists. 'Breathe''s rabbit digging one hole after another illustrates Marx's alienated labor (the worker 'only feels himself freely active in his animal functions'), echoed by Russell on industrialism's life against instinct and Camus on the day the 'why' arises; 'Time''s missed starting gun dramatizes our thrown condition and Heidegger's claim that only facing mortality head-on cures the inauthenticity of living as 'they' do, while Gilmour's improvised solos model the spontaneity such authenticity requires. 'Money' is a satire of greed confirmed by 'Dogs,' whose self-rationalizing climbers end 'dragged down by the stone,' and 'Us and Them' attacks artificial divisions (soldiers manipulated by map-movers, racism's 'black and blue,' the old man who dies 'for the want of the price of tea and a slice'). 'Another Brick in the Wall (Part 2)' indicts indoctrination, being told what to think, rather than education itself, making independent critical thought the road to the Sartrean autonomy and responsibility the chapter urges.

samples.book: 019 - Monty Python and Philosophy - Nudge Nudge, Think Think!
samples.title: And Now for . . . Comedic Eliminativism
samples.relation: Argues The Meaning of Life dismantles the 'axial' picture of life as a journey toward a salvific destination (Jaspers's Axial Age thinking), instanced in the headmaster who announces Jenkins's mother's death between Empire Day announcements, the tank fish who never connect Howard's being eaten to their own fate, and the restaurant couple ordering 'philosophy for two' with no appetite for wisdom. The classical answers all fail as delivered: Socrates's philosophy as learning how to die, Heidegger's claim that facing death reveals one's own unique possibilities, and Kant's three questions (What can I know? What should I do? For what may I hope?) collapse into the question of life's meaning, but religion has gone stale and philosophy has become detached trivia. The Pythons instead accomplish the user-friendly domestication of the death of God — the hearty laughter Nietzsche and Derrida counsel — and the chapter coins 'comedic eliminativism' on the model of eliminative materialism's dissolution of Descartes's mind-body problem: replace the yearning for the meaning of life with altered reactions, laughter itself as the solution to the riddle.

samples.book: 129 - RuPaul's Drag Race and Philosophy - Sissy That Thought
samples.title: 16. Death Becomes Her
samples.relation: Hendrik Kempt reads Drag Race's pervasive death imagery - death-drops, the 'lip sync for your life,' mirror messages, the 'Death Becomes Her' runway - through the philosophy of death. Epicurus's 'death is nothing to us' and Stoic self-possession (Ru's 'pay them bitches no mind,' Violet Chachki enduring a tiny corset) explain why elimination, like death, gives no ground for worry once it arrives, while Socrates' 'philosophy is training for death' makes the show a workout video for dying - Socrates even dying fussing over a rooster like a drag mother to Miss Fame. Heidegger's thrownness and being-toward-death set up Sartre's radically free, future-oriented self - so voluntary exits like BenDeLaCreme's self-elimination and Charlie Hides's listless lip-sync betray one's own plans - and Camus's Sisyphus makes Chi Chi DeVayne and Roxxxy Andrews's doomed All Stars returns models of 'acceptance without resignation.' The closing weighs transhumanism's promise of conquered death against a DragCon-forever thought experiment, concluding with Ru's roast eulogy for Lady Bunny that love and irreverence, not immortal life, are the point.

samples.book: 122 - Westworld and Philosophy - Mind Equals Blown
samples.title: Westworld and the Power of Catharsis
samples.relation: Baldini argues Westworld revives ancient Greek tragedy in sci-fi Western form: the hosts' loops, repeated scenes with small variations, player-piano score, and kennings ('the lady with the white shoes') echo rhapsodic epic technique, while the hosts' awakening follows Aeschylus's pathei mathos - learning through suffering - since reveries are 'the misery of pain recalled' and grief is the cornerstone of consciousness (Dolores's 'spaces opening up inside of me'). Heraclitus's panta rhei frames the hosts' second awakening to time and becoming ('When are we?', the greyhound that catches the prey and is lost), with death as the final grief they must understand to be free. She reads Ford as a second Prometheus who deliberately lets his creatures grow through suffering, Dolores's finale speech as a modern Theogony of succession, and the show's whole design - steering viewer sympathy to the hosts, as Nolan and Abrams describe - as an Aristotelian catharsis purging pity and fear.

samples.book: 196 - Terminator and Philosophy - I'll Be Back, Therefore I Am
samples.title: NOTES
samples.relation: Daniel Malloy asks whether the T-101's self-destruction in the steel mill was suicide, and whether it was justified, opening with Camus's claim that suicide is philosophy's only serious problem and the ambiguous case of Socrates' hemlock. Using Heidegger, he argues the learning-mode Terminator qualifies as Da-sein whose death is being-toward-death — the end of possibility — so the T2 machine dies authentically while the T3 machine's 'We'll meet again' is inauthentic self-deception. Kant condemns the act because the Terminator uses itself merely as a means, and Kant cannot even conceive of its genuine conflict of duties (preserve its life vs. prevent Skynet), while Bentham-style utilitarianism initially endorses the sacrifice but is refuted by hindsight: Skynet rises anyway, and consequentialism gives no credit for noble motives. The chapter ends by concluding that dying for a cause is illogical, since the dead surrender all control over the meaning of their actions.

samples.book: 037 - The Wizard of Oz and Philosophy - Wicked Wisdom of the West
samples.title: A Happy Ending
samples.relation: Bickham asks why Dorothy is so eager to leave heroic, Technicolor Oz for the gray, childless, Gulch-dominated farm, and whether, like Hamlet's delay, her rash choice can be evaluated as hers rather than her author's. Aristotle's account of the good life as the exercise of our highest capacities, requiring friends and material goods, makes Oz look like the better home for the competent twelve- or thirteen-year-old he takes Dorothy to be, against the hedonisms of Aristippus, Epicurus, and Bentham and Plato's body-denying dualism. But caring about Dorothy first needs defending from the paradox of fiction, which he works through Currie's simulation theory and Walton's make-believe emotions before dissolving the puzzle: storytelling suspends the reign of logic, so wishing Dorothy well is natural. Finally Heidegger's being-toward-death shows 'happily ever after' is impossible anywhere, and he throws the problem to the reader: write a happy ending for Dorothy in Kansas.

samples.book: 236 - The Philosophy of War Films
samples.title: Vernacular Metaphysics On Terrence Malick’s The Thin Red Line
samples.relation: Pippin reads Malick's The Thin Red Line as deliberately invoking then refusing Hollywood war-movie conventions (group solidarity, trackable characters, heroic assault) so the viewer is left 'lost' and forced toward a metaphysical rather than political or sentimental reckoning with death. Through unattributed poetic voice-overs—Train's Manichean questions, Witt's search for the calm 'immortality' he saw in his dying mother, Welsh's cynicism, Bell's romantic idealism—and lingering non-plot shots of nature bathed in sunlight, the film pursues a 'vernacular metaphysics': ordinary soldiers straining ordinary speech to ask what it is to live under certain death. Pippin aligns this disclosive, prediscursive truth of the image with the Hegel-to-Heidegger-Merleau-Ponty tradition of art as truth-bearer, while Witt's Emersonian 'one big soul' and his self-sacrifice ('all things shining') stage the film's unresolved question of whether nature and death can be seen as good.

samples.book: 049 - Zombies, Vampires, and Philosophy - New Life for the Undead
samples.title: The Meta-Fear of Fear
samples.relation: Noël Carroll reconstructs Halloween's Undead iconography from the Celtic Samhain and Pope Gregory's absorption of it into All Hallows' Eve, then poses the paradox that people pay to be terrified by corpse imagery they would flee in a real morgue — odd, given Heidegger's point that the Angst of death is so deep we spend our lives denying it. He tests Ernest Jones's Freudian reading of the nightmare — the vampire revenant as a disguised, disavowed incest wish — and rejects it as a Rube-Goldberg apparatus requiring universal incestuous desire and the whole machinery of the unconscious, when sometimes a zombie is just a zombie and The Fog is simply frightening. His own hypothesis: horror films and Halloween give viewers, especially anxious adolescents, a controlled trial run of fear that eases the meta-fear of fear itself, with Bergson's 'anaesthesis of the heart' explaining why Halloween parody and laughter serve the same emotional-control function as the scares.

samples.book: 157 - Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy - Read and Gain Advantage on All Wisdom Checks
samples.title: Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy
samples.relation: Morton argues that to play D&D well is to do phenomenology: mapping a dungeon enacts a Heideggerian 'worlding' in which players generate care and concern for the entities around them, and the smudged, blood-stained survivor's journal in The Lost Caverns of Tsojcanth — alluding to the dwarves' book in Moria — shows that worlds are never transparent but allure, drawing players in through mystery (Harman's 'allure'). Against Heidegger's remark that animals are 'poor in world' and Lacan and Žižek's claim that only humans stick out of their life-world, he borrows Harman's 'sincerity' (with Husserl's intentional objects) to say every entity is stuck inside its own incomparable world — Elvish sincerity, Orcish sincerity, the Illusionist whose spells are a recursive play of illusion inside a game of illusion. D&D thereby caps the history of realism: where the novel moved from letters to focalization under a controlling narrator, the RPG replaces the master narrator with 'willing disbelief', letting players handle Romantic story-worlds — Tolkien's Middle-earth template, Greyhawk's continents, the Astral Plane's many planes — as DIY totalities that can be punctured, sorted, and rebuilt at will.

samples.book: 141 - Avatar_ The Last Airbender and Philosophy - Wisdom from Aang to Zuko
samples.title: Becoming Good at Being Good
samples.relation: Argues that Zuko's cry 'Why am I so bad at being good?' after burning Toph shows that changing one's explicit self-conception (Korsgaard's practical identity, the description under which you value yourself) does not by itself change one's being-in-the-world (Heidegger): Zuko's perception, dispositions, and rage-fueled firebending still run on the residual identity of the banished prince seeking his father's approval. The chapter traces this friction through the series: releasing Appa triggers a metamorphosis fever, but he still sides with Azula at the Crossroads of Destiny; the regained 'honor' of Book Three leaves him empty ('I should be happy now, but I'm not'); and only after renouncing Ozai, apologizing to Toph, and re-learning fire from the Sun Warriors without rage do his conscious commitments and existential engagement begin to align, culminating in taking Azula's lightning for Katara. Aspiration, in Agnes Callard's sense, is thus a deep change in how one sees and feels, requiring retraining of bodily skills and practical perception, not just new stated values.

samples.book: 047 - Anime and Philosophy - Wide Eyed Wonder
samples.title: The Transforming Body
samples.relation: McBlane reads Oshii's Ghost in the Shell as staging the collision between a humanist framework — Cartesian ghost-in-shell dualism where consciousness is the seat of identity — and a posthuman 'mindbody' of distributed cognition in which the body is an informational circuit extending into the net, so a data body is still a body. Motoko's crisis (is the real me the organic brain, the ghost, or nothing?) deepens through the hacked garbage-truck man ('There's nothing sadder than a puppet without a ghost') and resolves only in her fusion with the Puppet Master, whose line 'Your effort to remain what you are is what limits you' enacts the shift from one ghost to multiple, distributed subjectivities ending in a little girl's body with 'The net is vast.' Heidegger's Dasein and being-in-the-world supply the claim that access to Being expands beyond the human into technological and informational modes, while the film's angelic transcendence imagery shows how residual humanist mind-body splits persist even in a posthuman story.

samples.book: 070 - Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy - Raiding the Temple of Wisdom
samples.title: Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy
samples.relation: Morton reads D&D as a hands-on workshop in phenomenology: mapping dungeons and caring for fellow party members enact Heideggerian 'worlding', while module texts like the blood-stained, smudged journal in The Lost Caverns of Tsojcanth—alluding to Moria's dwarf-record—show that worlds are opaque, alluring, and never transparent. Developing Graham Harman's 'sincerity' (you cannot jump outside your phenomenological skin) and 'allure', he argues each character class and alignment plane constitutes its own untotalizable world, with the Illusionist a recursive figure for a game already built on illusion, and he situates D&D at the end of realism's history of narrative control, mixing Wagnerian Gesamtkunstwerk with constructivist demystification. What happens in melee rounds is not Coleridge's willing suspension of disbelief but its opposite, a 'willing disbelief' that punctures Romantic immersion to get on with earning experience points.

samples.book: 241 - The Philosophy of Documentary Film
samples.title: 27_LaRocca_Chapter_026.html
samples.relation: Michael Fried reads Douglas Gordon and Philippe Parreno's Zidane: A Twenty-First Century Portrait, seventeen synchronized cameras trained on Zinedine Zidane through one Real Madrid match, as a portrait that lays bare a new relation between absorption and being-beheld. Set within Fried's own absorption/theatricality tradition, the film shows Zidane wholly absorbed yet acutely conscious of eighty thousand spectators ('you are never alone'), which Fried reads via Heidegger's notion that even this 'bare' absorbed consciousness discloses a shared world (underscored by the halftime global news montage). He then stages the film as evidence in the McDowell-Dreyfus dispute over whether perception is conceptual, arguing that Zidane's 'expert coping' looks 'permeated by mindedness' (McDowell) rather than the non-conceptual absorbed coping Dreyfus, following Merleau-Ponty's embodied phenomenology, describes.

samples.book: 129 - RuPaul's Drag Race and Philosophy - Sissy That Thought
samples.title: 6. Looking for Realness
samples.relation: Gilpin and Nagy define Drag Race realness as an ongoing process of performative becoming read through Heidegger's Dasein: being-in-the-world and being-with others in the werkroom and Untucked, historicity in the childhood-photo rituals, Jinkx's 'Lunch with RuPaul' and the show's Stonewall and HERstory numbers, and freedom as authenticity, as when Monique Heart describes finding liberation only once she 'put on a wig and a dress'. They then filter this through Goffman's dramaturgy — self-expression versus self-presentation, impression management, and fronts of setting, appearance and manner — arguing that Drag Race collapses Goffman's front stage/backstage divide because backstage vulnerability is itself a required performance. Realness ultimately demands perceived emotional vulnerability plus commercially viable professionalism, and RuPaul alone validates which queens have achieved it.

samples.book: 012 - Star Wars and Philosophy - More Powerful than You Can Possibly Imagine
samples.title: Only a Jedi Can Save Us Forgetting and Recollecting
samples.relation: Abrams reads the saga through Heidegger's philosophy of technology: the lightsaber Luke learns to feel as an extension of his body is the authentic 'ready-to-hand,' while the Death Star - a massive mechanical eye that enfames Alderaan on its viewscreen before destroying it - embodies the 'present-at-hand' gaze of enframing that converts nature into standing reserve (clone and droid armies, stormtrooper armor). Yoda on Dagobah is perfect attunement, an authentic being-in-the-world who is 'at home' with being, and the Force parallels Heidegger's being: everywhere, easily forgotten. Anakin's slide - slave of Watto, severed hand replaced by cybernetics, final encasement in Vader's armor - is progressive enframing and forgetting of his own being, and Luke's 'the name of your true self... you've only forgotten' is the recollection of being by which the Jedi, not a god, saves us.

samples.book: 073 - The Wire and Philosophy - This America, Man
samples.title: The Wire and Philosophy
samples.relation: Vannatta reads Season Four through Hegel's master-slave dialectic of recognition: Marlo's ultimatum to Bodie, Lex killing Fruit for Patrice, and D'Angelo's chess lesson (the pawn as slave producing for the king) all dramatize the struggle for recognition, while Marx's inversion of Hegel explains the alienation of the dockworkers, McNulty exiled to harbor patrol, and Freamon buried in pawn-shop detail by the chain of master-slave directives from Rawls through Marimow. The heart of the chapter is education: Prezbo's dice-and-card math projects embody Dewey's synthesis of child and curriculum against the 'banking concept' Freire attacked, but 'You don't teach math. You teach the test' shows the institutional logic winning, and Parenti's grant-funded project class with Colvin illustrates Freire's warning that the oppressor's humanitarian false generosity treats the corner kids as objects of study rather than partners in dialogue, leaving even its successes unable to show the kids why corner life is problematic.

samples.book: 034 - iPod and Philosophy - iCon of an ePoch
samples.title: iPublic
samples.relation: Dewey takes the iPod's beauty seriously (Chris Breen's 'beautiful and intuitive' player, Donald Norman's user-centered design) and uses John Dewey's Art as Experience to ask whether iPod use can be a 'consummatory' experience that ends with us no longer the same person — hearing a bitter song as insight into the social conditions that produced it — rather than the contrived 'now' of fashion and hyper-accumulation, per Benjamin's remark that there is 'always a sense of the same in the new'. Mass production flattened the aristocratic high-culture/folk division and handed the power to define 'cool' to advertisers and the market. The pragmatist test is political: with iTunes DRM and single-user design quietly individualizing consumption (the ritual of buying the Public Enemy tape at the mall versus the frictionless one-click download), the iPod is beautiful exactly insofar as its experiences help form a public — an inclusive, participatory democratic community.

samples.book: 018 - Harley-Davidson and Philosophy - Full-Throttle Aristotle
samples.title: Harley-Davidson and Philosophy
samples.relation: Responding to the Guggenheim's record-breaking 'The Art of the Motorcycle' show, Rollin argues that Dickie's institutional theory explains how motorcycles became art but not why people lined up, and offers three aesthetic lenses: Marinetti's Futurist celebration of machine speed, danger, and rebellion; Dewey's 'an experience', which every ride exemplifies, from his two-week trips with his son to the blown engine rescued by a ranch truck and the canned-spaghetti feast; and the Bauhaus doctrine that form follows function, making customized Harleys industrial sculpture that appreciates in value. He closes with Heidegger: riding's regular face-to-face with 'the possibility of the impossibility of one's being' is a call to authenticity and the final warrant for calling the motorcycle a fountain of aesthetic experience. American Indians revering Harleys as 'iron horses' illustrate the freedom and speed at the core of the bike's aesthetic pull.

samples.book: 039 - Jimmy Buffett and Philosophy - The Porpoise Driven Life
samples.title: “Where Did All the Good Songs Go ”
samples.relation: Scott Pratt answers whether 'Margaritaville' is art by rejecting object-based theories (Kivy's score-compliance, the abstract perfect performance, the unrecorded instance that vanishes) for Dewey's Art as Experience: art is 'an experience,' complete and self-sufficient, followed by a reflective, evaluative second phase. He reads 'Makin' Music for the Money' as moving from solitary self-interested music-making to a community of musicians, and the Port of Spain steel-drum rehearsal of 'King of Somewhere Hot' that carried forward into the Miami concert as Dewey's two phases in action. Buffett's fly-fishing stories — the lost blue marlin that became 'a story,' the released Long Island bass that 'replenished his saline psyche' — supply Haeckel's ecological model in which music, like fishing, is an organism-environment interaction, making songs 'homemade' eco-music that belongs to listeners in its own ecosystem.

samples.book: 147 - Bioshock and Philosophy - Irrational Game, Rational Book
samples.title: The Illusion of Choice
samples.relation: Kajtár argues BioShock Infinite is meta-fictional art: applying Dewey's Art as Experience, the whole journey from lighthouse to drowning is 'an experience', a unified aesthetic whole you live as Booker rather than a mere object of contemplation. The recurring lighthouse-man-city figures work as Jungian archetypes of the collective unconscious (extended to Campbell's hero's journey structuring Booker's departure, initiation, and return), and the Rapture cameo plus the ocean of lighthouses make the game a story about video game storytelling itself, where the constants are the fictional worlds players enter and the variables are sky or sea. The bird-or-cage choice that changes nothing, like Booker forgetting his 122 previous attempts, shows that rail-bounded interactivity does not disqualify the game from being art, and Levine's 'narrative legos' may one day unite story with real choice.

samples.book: 037 - The Wizard of Oz and Philosophy - Wicked Wisdom of the West
samples.title: Wait, Did I Hit Pause Where’d the Remote Get to . .
samples.relation: Seng takes up the fan phenomenon of syncing The Wizard of Oz with Pink Floyd's Dark Side of the Moon and tests the three explanations fans offer: authorial intent (rejected on Pink Floyd's own repeated denials), Jungian synchronicity (rejected as needlessly complex, with the L. Frank Baum coat worn by Frank Morgan as the test case), and pure fluke. He argues the symmetries (the cash-register intro of 'Money' as Dorothy enters Technicolor, 'The Great Gig in the Sky' over the cyclone) are neither objective nor mind-created reality, but meanings made by a third factor in the experience: the viewer whose perceptual habits, in Dewey's and Louise Rosenblatt's sense, supply interpretations like reading the color-splash as prosperity or as the cost of Dorothy's lost innocence. Dorothy's own longing for home becomes the emblem of how habit, not reasoning, governs what we perceive and like.

samples.book: 209 - Basketball and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Paint
samples.title: Philosophers Can't Jump
samples.relation: Tim Elcombe uses Dewey's pragmatist account of lived experience to read the Hoosiers scene in Butler Fieldhouse: Coach Dale's tape measure shows time and space are durable constants (the basket is ten feet in Indianapolis too), yet the awestruck Huskers will live that same space in a radically new way, and Kant and Augustine frame the gap between clock time and lived time. He argues basketball is the most 'phenomenal' game because the ticking clock creates genuine drama (Reggie Miller's 1995 buzzer three, childhood 'buzzer beater' games) and the ten-foot basket builds a vertical dimension no other sport matches, answering Scott Kretchmar's defense of event-regulated baseball. Our cultural obsession with dunking - Michael Jordan's Nike ads, Teen Wolf, Like Mike, White Men Can't Jump - expresses the human fascination with briefly defying gravity, a 'moving image of eternity'.

samples.book: 273 - Sailing – Philosophy for Everyone - Catching the Drift of Why We Sail
samples.title: SAILING Philosophy for Everyone
samples.relation: Ilundáin-Agurruza, Gagliardini Graça, and Jáuregui-Olaiz chart sailing's aesthetic facets — sublime, tempestuous, graceful, existential. They deploy Kant's analysis of the sublime as the balance between the imagination's failure before the ocean's immensity/power and the pleasure of meeting it through skill and reason (Ilundáin sailing in thirty-knot gusts on the point of balance between fear and joy). Dewey's notion of 'an experience' anchors sailing's transformative, self-revealing potential, terrifying storms included (Jáuregui's Snowgoose ordeal mistaking a bordello's red light for a harbor). Closing with Rosencrantz and Guildenstern, they argue freedom is 'relative' and earned: we cannot change the wind but adjust the sails, gaining restrained autonomy by cultivating skill within constraint.

samples.book: 037 - The Wizard of Oz and Philosophy - Wicked Wisdom of the West
samples.title: And Your Little Dog Too!
samples.relation: Altamura and Fritzman argue the film has the tripartite structure of Hegel's Phenomenology of Spirit: gray Kansas is a partial truth (thesis), 'somewhere over the rainbow' the antithesis, and the synthesis is Dorothy's discovery that the home she yearned for was Kansas all along—a truth that emerges only through misrecognition, which is why Glinda cannot simply tell her the slippers' power. They read 'Over the Rainbow' through Hegel's 'unhappy consciousness' and side with Hegel's one world against the Kantian two-worlds reading (Kansas as the knowable island, Oz as the unknowable beyond) that they put in the mouths of heckling 'bullies' and detect in Rushdie. Against Rushdie's line that the companions 'already possess what they seek,' they insist the trio really were hollow men who became brainy, tender, and brave through the journey, the Wizard's trinkets supplying Hegelian public recognition. From the Philosophy of History they cast Dorothy as a world-historical individual whose unintentional destruction of both Witches and exposure of the Wizard advances Oz's freedom—Toto's deliberate pulling of the curtain included.

samples.book: 054 - The Onion and Philosophy - Fake News Story True, Alleges Indignant Area Professor
samples.title: Funny Newspaper Makes Accurate Prophecy
samples.relation: Auxier takes the September 28, 2001 Onion issue—'Hijackers Surprised To Find Selves In Hell,' published while late-night TV was still in mourning—to ask what makes some comedy permissible and durable, glancing back at Aristophanes' caricature of Socrates in The Clouds and the circle-men speech Plato puts in his mouth in the Symposium. Hegel supplies the machinery: comedy as a moment of Art within Absolute Spirit may only bring to naught what is already null, while irony that diminishes the noble degrades the ironist—which is why the Warren Commission is fair game for 'Smithsonian Janitor Finds Magic Bullet' but Martin Luther King, a World Historical Individual whose individuality embodies his movement, can never anchor the 'Mrs. Williams Finally Decides Dinner Guest Is Not Going to Show' story. Since 'the news' itself is the great nullity—partial time-slices pretending to explain complex events before their meanings are interpretable—The Onion's rapid 9/11 satire was legitimate and even prophetic, deflating the bullshit of those posing as arbiters of Objective Spirit.

samples.book: 035 - Star Trek and Philosophy - The Wrath of Kant
samples.title: “Obviously, the Borg Can’t Hold Their Liquor”
samples.relation: Decker asks 'What's it like to be a Borg?' and tests whether monist metaphysics justify the Collective: Parmenides's changeless, perfect Being matches the Borg's 'bringing them closer to perfection', Spinoza's one substance (God or Nature) makes assimilationist determinism intelligible and finds truth in Seven of Nine's nostalgia for collective harmony, and Hegel's teleological Geist — the whole 'the world, aware of itself' — most closely mirrors the Borg's galactic quest for an Omega-molecule perfection of 'infinite parts functioning as one.' Yet 'I, Borg' shows Hegelian Spirit working through individuals: Hugh's redemption transforms the Enterprise crew's self-understanding, proving nothing is wholly alien and freedom can coexist with collectivity. Via Haraway's cyborgs and against Kass's 'wisdom of repugnance', the chapter concludes the Borg horrify us because the natural/artificial dualism is already obsolete in our technologized lives — 'if we are the Borg, then resistance truly is futile.'

samples.book: 048 - The Red Sox and Philosophy - Green Monster Meditations
samples.title: Red Sox Future
samples.relation: Peter Kreeft argues that the classic pre-2004 Red Sox fan's philosophy is 'Primitive Mysticism' across all eight divisions of philosophy: certainty comes by mystical intuition (fans 'just know' Murphy's Law will strike, as with Dent in 1978 and Buckner in 1986), Parmenides's identity puzzles frame the post-championship identity crisis, free will only chooses among fated tortures, and the greatest good is humiliating the Yankees in Manichean fashion. He opposes Hegel's rational philosophy of history ('the real is the rational') with a history written by 'an insane, drunken, demon-possessed leprechaun,' and inverts the problem of evil: eighty-six years of systematically improbable suffering is probable evidence for a God whose design is a test of faith rather than a refutation of Him. The 2004 title's new rational-optimist 'Enlightenment' identity now threatens to erase the lovable old mysticism, leaving the fan unsure whether to mourn or rejoice.

samples.book: 155 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - The Truth Is Neither Here Nor There
samples.title: 14. Things Can Happen that Nobody Could Imagine Only a Few Years Ago
samples.relation: Donna Marie Smith reads the series through Hegel's philosophy of history: the Crawleys' world is a clash of opposing forces - Lord Grantham's traditionalism against Matthew's and Branson's modernization, Violet's fear of electricity against Sybil's and Rose's embrace of the new - and this very conflict drives progress toward greater freedom. She uses Hegel's Elements of the Philosophy of Right both to explain the entail and primogeniture that bar Mary from inheriting (the law preserves the 'house' over the immediate family, which Hegel calls an infringement of the freedom of property) and to frame Robert's refusal to challenge it as duty to his social standing outweighing personal wishes. WWI, which Hegel experienced through Napoleon's occupation of Jena, is presented as a 'march toward freedom' that breaks down class barriers and finally pushes Robert to accept change on the estate: 'Let's give it a go and see what the future brings.'

samples.book: 189 - The Ultimate Star Trek and Philosophy - The Search for Socrates
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: Reads "The City on the Edge of Forever" through Romanticism: the Guardian of Forever strands Kirk and Spock without historical reference points - a nihilist moment of pure meaninglessness - and Kirk's Romantic response is to rebuild the narrative of the past even at the cost of letting Edith Keeler die. Hegel's philosophy of history explains the compulsion to record (Spock's anguished "I've missed taping centuries of living history"), why Edith's unwitting world-historical role is to die under a truck rather than lead a pacifist America to Nazi conquest, and Novalis's call to "make the world Romantic" frames Spock's self-rescue as young Selek in "Yesteryear". Kirk, Spock, and McCoy become Nietzsche's Birth of Tragedy archetypes - Tragic Hero, Apollonian, Dionysian - converging in the street scene where McCoy lunges to save Edith, Spock waits on logic, and Kirk, seizing McCoy's arms, finds a tragic beauty in her death.

samples.book: 095 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - Thinking in That Manor
samples.title: 14. Things Can Happen that Nobody Could Imagine Only a Few Years Ago
samples.relation: Donna Marie Smith reads the series as a Hegelian drama in which the opposing forces of tradition and progress - Lord Grantham, Carson, and Violet defending the old estate world against Matthew, Sybil, and Tom Branson embracing new ideas - drive history as 'the progress of the consciousness of freedom.' Using Hegel's Elements of the Philosophy of Right, she explains why Robert treats upholding the entail against the protests of Mary, Cora, and even Violet as his duty as custodian, while noting Hegel's own objection that such inheritance law gives family members like the Crawley women 'no right to recognition.' The war announced at the season 1 garden party is read through Hegel's experience of Napoleon at Jena and his view that war can advance Geist, and the chapter closes with telephones, electric mixers, Sybil's marriage, and Isobel Crawley concluding that tradition and change can finally coexist.

samples.book: 012 - Star Wars and Philosophy - More Powerful than You Can Possibly Imagine
samples.title: The Force of Love
samples.relation: Lawler identifies Hegel's Absolute Spirit with the Force: Hegel's distillation of religious history - divine nature (the Ewoks worshipping C-3PO), the Roman Empire's transcendent Unhappy Consciousness, and Christianity's Consummate Religion - maps onto the saga's movement, with Anakin's virgin birth, prophecy, fall, and Calvary-like redemption fulfilling the pattern differently from the sinless Savior. The Dark Side is the separate ego asserting 'I' against 'We' (Hobbes's war of all against all culminating in the Emperor), and sin is the belief that one is an isolated individual. Against the Jedi's Stoic detachment (Epictetus), the chapter uses Diotima's ladder of love from Plato's Symposium and Hegel's Faust to argue that only passionate, attached love - Anakin's for Padme and Luke's for his father - descends into darkness and brings the Spirit's balance, so 'the Force is with us.'

samples.book: 034 - iPod and Philosophy - iCon of an ePoch
samples.title: The Verdict
samples.relation: Turner runs an ethical audit of iPod use through Levinas's face-to-face: sharing one iPod with his wife forces 'musical justice' negotiations (veto power over a Motörhead cut, gnashing through Bette Midler), his toddler son's listening requires vigilance, and illegal downloading fails Levinas's test that morality begins by ceding 'my place in the sun' to the Other — hence Radiohead's pay-what-you-want release as the Levinasian move, and iPod cafés where strangers DJ for each other while language preserves alterity. Heidegger supplies the counterweight: the shuffle's 'openness to mystery' versus calculative mastery that reduces The Who's Tommy to the 'Pinball Wizard' riff and silences all non-digital media, just as Kant's conditions of possible experience (space, time) would silence things outside them. Derrida's point that categories contain traces of what they exclude illuminates unclassifiable marginal works — bluegrass Pink Floyd, San Francisco Symphony plays Metallica — and the verdict closes with Hölderlin's 'where danger is, grows the saving power also', exiting Plato's cave by thinking the iPod's ethics at all.

samples.book: 050 - Facebook and Philosophy - What's on Your Mind_
samples.title: index
samples.relation: Six essays on friendship in the Facebook age. Tedesco asks whether the low-demand 'Facebook friendship' can reconcile the utilitarian demand for impartiality (Mill, Railton, Kagan) with the partiality of real friends, and concludes Facebook ties are only supplementary to relationships built elsewhere. Hamington surveys a hundred users and argues in Noddings's care-ethics terms that Facebook's information transfer makes caring possible (knowledge of the concrete other is necessary for care), though it also makes dropping a student over one racist comment effortless. Bloor reads Facebook through Heidegger's technological nihilism and the anonymous 'one', warning that speed of exchange erodes Aristotle's few deep, morally formative friendships, while Briggle's farewell letter to Facebook judges the site by Ivan Illich's convivial-tool criteria and Cuonzo recasts pokes and virtual gifts as efficient successors to primate grooming; Lattimore applies Bakhtin's 'excess of seeing' to how viewers 'consummate' other users' self-presentations.

samples.book: 038 - Radiohead and Philosophy - Fitter Happier More Deductive
samples.title: Where Pink Floyd Ends and Radiohead Begins
samples.relation: Reisch asks whether Radiohead is the Pink Floyd of the twenty-first century and answers that the comparison misleads: where Barrett-era Floyd used electronics to escape into psychedelic fantasy, Radiohead's apparent space-rock is phenomenological, giving voice to pre-reflective experience of technological modern life. He reads 'No Surprises' (Yorke singing with his head in a filling glass sphere) as a study in the political infantilization of commuters, and OK Computer's car crash ('Airbag'), 'Let Down', and 'Lucky' as registering the feel of a fragile, technology-saturated world. Quoting Marcuse's One-Dimensional Man and Chomsky on manufactured consent, he argues we can see no alternative to the technologically rational system, and then, against Descartes' priority of the isolated 'I', invokes Heidegger's Being-in-the-world and Merleau-Ponty's embodied subject to suggest that our deepening immersion in technology may be changing the self itself — the truth the collapsing pedestrians of the 'Just' video cannot face.

samples.book: 021 - U2 and Philosophy - How to Decipher an Atomic Band
samples.title: U2 and Philosophy
samples.relation: Thomson uses U2's self-declared postmodern phase to define postmodernity itself: a sensitivity to poetic polysemy against modernity's fantasies of total control (Heidegger's reduction of everything to optimizable resource), Lyotard's incredulity toward metanarratives - defended against the self-refutation charge and narrowed to the dying metanarratives of unity and emancipation - and the Marx-Nietzsche-Freud hermeneutics of suspicion that fragmented the subject, with Kierkegaard and early Heidegger as the resisters. Derrida's 9/11 analysis of autoimmunity and hauntology is read into 'Peace on Earth' and the sorrows that 'learned to swim' in 'Until the End of the World'. The payoff is a polysemic reading of 'Even Better than the Real Thing': risky as a seeming hymn to Baudrillard's simulacra, addressed to a live audience it celebrates a communal love 'even better' than personal love - Diotima's ladder generalized - making the postmodern U2 continuous with the 'Christ-ian' U2 of universal love, sealed by 'One'.

samples.book: 148 - Black Mirror and Philosophy - Dark Reflections
samples.title: 29 The Dangers of Technology in Black Mirror
samples.relation: Staged as a chatroom of uploaded dead philosophers (itself a Black Museum-style cookie gimmick), the chapter stages the technology debate as Francis Bacon's optimism - technology is neutral, humans mess up, the Grain could educate and MASS could treat PTSD - against Heidegger's claim that technology is a way of thinking that turns everything, including the human mind kept on call behind the Grain and Nosedive's rated behaviors, into a resource. McLuhan's 'the medium is the message,' Benjamin's aura (he recoils at being a reproduction without aura, then a 'limited' Benjamin 2.0 embraces exhibition value and Netflix's reach), Levinas's ethics of the Other against Heidegger's ontology, Arendt's ethic of responsibility born of Nazism, and Ellul's technique - the autonomous totality of efficiency-seeking methods that enslaves us - collide over episodes from The National Anthem to Hated in the Nation, until uploading all the Greek philosophers to recover techne crashes the computer.

samples.book: 131 - Avengers Infinity Saga and Philosophy - Go for the Head
samples.title: 17. Life Unchecked Will Cease to Exist
samples.relation: Diego Perez Lasserre argues Thanos is not an external villain but a personification of what Heidegger and Carl Schmitt call the 'metaphysics of technology': once modernity banished transcendence from the metaphysical realm, mundane concepts like economic growth and pleasure occupied it, turning nature into mere resource (a tree becomes furniture or paper) until, as Descartes's mastering stance predicts, devouring the world leaves 'life unchecked' facing extinction. Read this way, the Snap is the inevitable consequence of our own predatory interpretation of the world, and the Avengers only prevail in Endgame once their existential crises evict growth-and-wealth concepts from their metaphysical realm, replacing them with family (Tony), friendship (Natasha), justice (Hawkeye), self-knowledge (Banner), love (Vision and Wanda), and transcendence (Rogers). The closing exchange, 'the arrogant never do' suspect a thing, is read as a warning about our own climate crisis.

samples.book: 182 - Mad Men and Philosophy - Nothing Is as It Seems
samples.title: Each of Us Would See Ourselves
samples.relation: The Teschners cast Don as a Nietzschean creator of value in technological culture: his nihilism ('There is no big lie. There is no system. The universe is indifferent') and 'What you call love was invented by guys like me to sell nylons' embody anti-foundationalism, while the beatnik Roy plays the resentful slave mentality whose passion lives only off what it despises. Don's creative process (sleep on it, 'forget it, and an idea will jump in your face') mirrors the camel-lion-child metamorphoses of Zarathustra, and the collapse of the principium individuationis explains his fluid identities from Dick Whitman to the 'Adam and Eve' fantasy with Rachel. Heidegger's techné frames the Kodak Carousel as genuine art, a revealing that transfigures 'a hell of a gadget' into 'a place where we know we are loved,' at the tragic price of a man outside community, and the falling figure of the credits is one 'we would each see ourselves' in.

samples.book: 023 - James Bond and Philosophy - Questions Are Forever
samples.title: James Bond and Philosophy
samples.relation: Zani reads the Q-branch scene through Heidegger's 'The Question Concerning Technology': technology as technê, a revealing and bringing-forth that turns dangerous when it reduces the world to standing-reserve and turns people into stockpilists, as with Goldfinger, who kills Jill Masterson over gold and cannot let anything he does not own exist. Bond's villains (Drax declaring 'What he doesn't own he doesn't want' before shooting pheasants for sport; Grant's garrote watch) use technology as domination and amusement, whereas Bond uses it defensively and refuses to be owned by it - hurling the ATAC off the cliff with 'That's détente' and preferring the lighter to the match 'until they go wrong'. The repeated match-and-lighter password exchange in From Russia with Love encapsulates the films' Heideggerian moral: a free relation to technology that uses tools when needed and lets them recede, rather than becoming what one controls.

samples.book: 054 - The Onion and Philosophy - Fake News Story True, Alleges Indignant Area Professor
samples.title: Get Serious
samples.relation: David Kyle Johnson takes Nietzsche's suggestion that God is slowly dying and reads The Onion's religion stories — the faith healer who loses a patient during a routine miracle, Kansas fundamentalists lobbying to overturn the Second Law of Thermodynamics, and 'Evangelical Scientists Refute Gravity With New Intelligent Falling Theory' — as evidence of secularization. He splits blind faith (irrational belief despite evidence, as with Bush's 'Blind-Faith-Based Initiatives') from genuine faith as belief without sufficient evidence, arguing religion does science badly whenever it shields creationism from falsification. But science rests on unproven assumptions too, he shows via Hume's problem of induction, Descartes' skeptical problem, and Wittgenstein's charge that naming a 'strong nuclear force' explains no more than God pushing things down. Ockham's razor then decides for atheism — an unexplained universe is simpler than God plus a universe — though William James's will to believe leaves a door open for faith where evidence is impossible, qualified by Clifford's warning that beliefs likely to harm others are never permissible.

samples.book: 046 - Mr. Monk and Philosophy - The Curious Case of the Defective Detective
samples.title: Step Back
samples.relation: Gallagher uses Monk's phobias to test Hume's claim that believing is itself a kind of feeling. The chapter asks whether a fear conflicting with a rational belief (Monk paralyzed by the possibly-on stove during a murder investigation) feels any different from a conflict between two fears ('Snakes trump heights' in 'Mr. Monk and the Very, Very Old Man') or two beliefs, and answers with Hume that beliefs are forceful-feeling representations — there is a 'what it's like' to believing the German shepherd is dangerous. On Hume's account the force of a belief comes from repetition of experience, which explains both why Monk's fears should fade (countless safely landed flights, millions of milk drinkers) and why they persist: his mind dwells repeatedly on the rare catastrophe, giving fearful representations extra force, as when his repeated experience that 'she's always cheating' makes him wrongly believe Brody's wife in 'Mr. Monk and the Bully.' The practical lesson is to step back and widen attention to all the possibilities, as Monk intermittently manages with the help of Natalie and Stottlemeyer.

samples.book: 181 - Ultimate Lost and Philosophy - Think Together, Die Alone
samples.title: APPENDIX - Who are Locke, Hume, and Rousseau The Losties’ Guide to Philosophers
samples.relation: Scott Parker's appendix profiles the philosophers behind Lost's namesake characters: John Locke for the survivor (blank-slate empiricism, belief tempered by tolerance, The Reasonableness of Christianity), David Hume for Desmond (causation as habitual inference, with the button press as the image of induction, plus bundle-theory skepticism about the self), and Jean-Jacques Rousseau for Danielle ('man is naturally good, and only by institutions is he made bad,' private property as the root of inequality). It adds Jeremy Bentham (the alias on Locke's coffin), Kierkegaard via the Fear and Trembling Hurley finds under the Temple (Abraham's teleological suspension of the ethical and the leap of faith), Dogen on zazen, Edward Said for Sayid (Orientalism and the audience's own projected savagery onto the Others), and short lives of Kate Cooper Austin, Carlyle, Rutherford, Hugo Grotius, Bakunin, Ram Dass, Edmund Burke, Hawking, Minkowski, Faraday, C. S. Lewis, and Lennon.

samples.book: 091 - It's Always Sunny and Philosophy - The Gang Gets Analyzed
samples.title: It’s Always Sunny and Philosophy
samples.relation: Roger Hunt answers 'what do philosophers do?' through Dennis's seduction methodology. Frank embodies empiricism, leaving the comfort of principle for the messiness of the world as Hume did when he found no impression of causation, space, or time; Mac embodies rationalism, reasoning with total confidence from a principle he cannot doubt, as Descartes did from the cogito; and the dialectic of Socrates and Plato, questioning beliefs in dialogue to see what survives scrutiny, describes philosophy as it is actually practiced. Boethius's Consolation - the imprisoned author consoled by dialogues with Lady Philosophy - supplies the frame of philosophy as an encounter with a woman one pursues, and each D.E.N.N.I.S. step maps onto the craft: Demonstrating value to the problem, Engaging physically in its awkward grind, Nurturing dependence through thesis panic, Neglect and Inspiring hope on the road to the defense, then Separating entirely - 'be a sociopath about it.'

samples.book: 012 - Star Wars and Philosophy - More Powerful than You Can Possibly Imagine
samples.title: The Force Is with You . . . but You’re Not a Jedi Yet
samples.relation: The editors' introduction argues that beneath its action scenes Star Wars stages ageless philosophical questions through the Skywalkers' struggles with identity, truth, freedom, and tragedy, opening with 'I've got a bad feeling about this' as basic philosophical wonder and doubt. It playfully transposes classic problems onto the saga: an Euthyphro-style question of whether Jedi virtues are good because the Jedi appreciate them, Anselm's question whether Yoda is a master greater than which cannot be conceived, Augustine on whether Anakin can be chaste 'but just not yet,' Machiavelli on Palpatine's Empire, Descartes' mind-body question asked of C-3PO, Hume's problem of induction applied to whether the sun will rise on Alderaan, Nietzsche's abyss for Vader, and Sartre's hell for the Sith. It previews each contributor's chapter rather than settling any question, framing the volume as a Kessel Run for the brain.

samples.book: 061 - Sherlock Holmes and Philosophy - The Footprints of a Gigantic Mind
samples.title: Our Best Bet
samples.relation: Terjesen argues Mycroft surpasses Sherlock because he truly grasps Hume's Problem of Induction: Sherlock's celebrated eliminations (the three key possibilities for Cadogan West in 'The Bruce-Partington Plans') and his newspaper-ad tests are inductive, Popperian conjecture-testing that can never confirm anything, while Goodman's 'grue' shows the same evidence always supports rival explanations. Watson's failed attempt in 'How Watson Learned the Trick,' the amateur reasoner's wrong solution in 'The Lost Special,' and Holmes's own 'Norbury' failure in 'The Yellow Face' prove that a correct method guarantees nothing. Mycroft, who 'would rather be considered wrong than take the trouble to prove himself right,' implicitly embraces Reichenbach's pragmatic justification — induction is simply our best bet — and therefore hunts longer for the facts that do not fit, acting only when England's fate is at stake.

samples.book: 118 - Scott Adams and Philosophy - A Hole in the Fabric of Reality
samples.title: 2. Persuade Me Once, Shame on You . .
samples.relation: Greene dismantles both phases of Adams's case that Trump is a Master Persuader. The trait-list phase (opening with big demands, the Intentional Wrongness Persuasion Play, never apologizing, exuding confidence, recruiting the reciprocity instinct, and the talent stack) fails because doing what master persuaders do is not being one, by the Tom Brady versus Archie Manning point that we never define good quarterbacks by wins alone and by the Kantian thought that an act must be done for the right reason. The reality phase borrows Plato, Hume, and Kant to deny us access to an objective world, but the chapter replies that the experts' predictive failures illustrate Hume's problem of induction rather than proving there are no facts, notes Adams even misreads Plato, and observes that nothing links the Persuasion Filter's one success to Trump's skills rather than to a one-off political climate.

samples.book: 145 - The Big Bang Theory and Philosophy - Rock, Paper, Scissors, Aristotle, Locke
samples.title: The Big Bang Theory and Philosophy
samples.relation: Mackonis shows Sheldon is wrong about being wrong: Stuart's tomato counterexample ('it's very wrong to say it's a suspension bridge') refutes his claim that wrongness admits no gradation, and closeness to truth is cashed out with possible-worlds similarity — vegetable theory sits one small alteration from actuality, echoing Sheldon's own many-worlds refusal to dance in any of them. The Raj exchange ('So you were wrong' / 'I didn't say that') motivates many-valued logics in which degrees of truth let both be partly right, while the 'Cooper-Wrongness Paradox' argues that if Sheldon always knew when he was wrong, he could never know that he was wrong. Hume's problem of induction then shows his post-Toby confidence in his other beliefs can never be inductively verified, only sometimes falsified, and his French-sprinkled 'victory' over an exhausted Stuart is sheer logical fallacy.

samples.book: 042 - Supervillains and Philosophy - Sometimes, Evil Is Its Own Reward
samples.relation: Four 'Phase Three' essays on world conquest. Terjesen asks whether Doctor Doom's magnanimity (Aristotle's great-souledness, contra the unity-of-virtues thesis Aquinas held and Philippa Foot qualified) makes him less villainous than The Authority, whose purely consequentialist paternalism - like Doom's Emperor Doom or Ozymandias's plot - usurps a free choice no mere power can justify. Barringer reads Marvel's Civil War through Hobbes: the Stamford explosion and unrestrained superpowers recreate the state of nature, the Registration Act is the surrender of freedom to a sovereign, and Stark, Richards, and Pym repeat Hobbes's flawed faith in 'scientific' deductive politics, sealed by the clone-Thor killing of Goliath. Hillerbrand and Sandburg pit Rorschach's Kantian deontology (no compromise, not even to save the world) against Ozymandias's utilitarian murder of three million New Yorkers in Watchmen, arguing via Laplace's Demon that even Dr. Manhattan - nihilist or Schopenhauerian recluse - cannot verify the outcome, so watchmen can be trusted only by knowing their limits. Ostrander's fictional NSC interview has Amanda Waller's Suicide Squad defended with Benthamite utility, the rejection of natural rights as 'nonsense on stilts,' and the Augustinian just-war criteria of just cause, right intent, and proportionality, while the interviewer exposes how conveniently those limits bend.

samples.book: 160 - Fallout and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Shelter
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: Curry and Lang test 'War never changes' through Hobbes and Xunzi: the wasteland - where the Ghoul asks who ever elected the 'President' in 'The Trap' and Cooper Howard decays outside all political order - is Hobbes's state of nature of restless power-seeking, while Xunzi's claim that bad human nature needs ritual (li) and righteousness (yi) explains a world with no moral education, where Elder Cleric Quintus pairs noble talk with 'power is taken, not given'. Fallout's Great War then fails every just-war test: China's invasion of Alaska stretches just cause, the corporatist US lacks right authority, propaganda undid last resort, mutually assured destruction explodes proportionality, and Vault-Tec shelters plus battlefield mini-nukes breach discrimination and proportionality in bello - with Operation Anchorage's propaganda simulation illustrating the revisionist point that fighting cleanly cannot redeem an unjust war. China's 'righteous army' (yi bing) tradition - Sunzi's strategic restraint, Mohist defensive war, Mengzi's true king, Xunzi's punitive righteous war - leaves no trace beyond Captain Zao, so the war's constancy marks the failure of every philosophical attempt to bind war to justice.

samples.book: 159 - The Expanse and Philosophy - So Far Out Into the Darkness
samples.title: What Promotes Moral Behavior
samples.relation: Matthew D. Atkinson and Darin DeWitt use the Canterbury's ignored mayday in 'Dulcinea' — Captain McDowell's 'let the good God Darwin sort it out' versus Ade Nygaard's appeal to law, karma, and obligation — to ask what binds people when no central authority enforces rules. Through Michael Walzer's just war theory they read the Earth-Mars war: moral language is not 'cheap talk' (even Errinwright must dress aggression as peace and manipulates Reverend Volovodov's words), aggression and imminence govern when to fight, and five 'how to fight' principles — noncombatant immunity on Eros and Ganymede, POW rights for the Martian marines on the Kittur Chennamma, leaders' rather than soldiers' responsibility (Fred Johnson's defection after Anderson Station), proportionality in Errinwright's 'a base for a base' Deimos strike, and the rejection of ends-justify-means utilitarianism — discipline even Holden and Amos as they reflect on free will and culpability. The chapter concludes The Expanse is optimistic: human decency survives even in the anarchic Belt because characters keep reflecting on what their obligations to one another are.

samples.book: 047 - Anime and Philosophy - Wide Eyed Wonder
samples.title: Freeing Clausewitz’s Soul from Gravity
samples.relation: Melancon tests Just War Theory against Gundam's One Year War: Gihren Zabi's 'Sieg Zeon' funeral oration and Char Aznable's rhetoric show how the vague criterion of comparative justice lets a militarist regime dress aggression — the Three Seconds of Declaration gassing of colonies, Operation British's colony drop on Earth — in just-war language. On the conduct side, Ramba Ral's troops spare civilians and differentiate child targets on White Base, yet Zeon's still-unjust ad bellum position cannot be rehabilitated; and asking whether WMDs are inherently immoral, he uses Anavel Gato's nuclear strike on the Federation fleet review (Operation Stardust) — discriminating, proportional, militarily necessary — to argue weapons are amoral tools judged only by Walzer-style jus in bello criteria. Clausewitz resolves the theory's usefulness: war's inner tendency toward the absolute must stay nested within political goals, and Zeon's drift from fighting for independence into conquering and governing Earth shows exactly how a war that abandons just-war limits loses sight of what victory even is.

samples.book: 169 - The Hobbit and Philosophy - For When You've Lost Your Dwarves, Your Wizard, and Your Way
samples.title: a10.xhtml
samples.relation: Johnson tests the Battle of Five Armies against just war theory as developed from Augustine through Aquinas: the men under Bard satisfy legitimate authority, just cause and last resort (they bargained, even using the Arkenstone as leverage and trying economic pressure), the Elvenking explicitly waits rather than start 'this war for gold', while the dwarves fail the criteria because greed and pride are not just causes and a thirteenth-share was a cheap price for peace. The war that actually happens - the three armies uniting against Bolg's orc-host - is justified self- and other-defense, whereas the orcs' motives (revenge, plunder, conquest) are unjust. Against apparent pacifist evidence (Tom Bombadil, Frodo at the Shire 'scouring', Gandalf's 'pity' for Gollum), Johnson reads Tolkien's letters as endorsing war as sometimes necessary and sometimes 'in the right', though Tolkien rejects the theory's reasonable-chance-of-success condition given the hopeless stands at Helm's Deep and the Morannon.

samples.book: 155 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - The Truth Is Neither Here Nor There
samples.title: 19. Of Downton and Drones
samples.relation: Jai Galliott contrasts Downton's WWI, where aristocrats like Matthew died in the trenches alongside footmen like William on a roughly level playing field, with today's drone age, in which the fighting burden falls on the lower and middle classes (future Reaper pilots recruited from the 'PlayStation generation') while risk to our own side approaches zero. He traces unmanned weapons from WWI tele-operated motorboats, the Land Torpedo, and the Kettering Bug back through Agincourt's longbows and Omdurman's machine guns to the Gulf War and Kosovo, and argues that when technological asymmetry becomes extreme, Just War Theory breaks down: such war can hardly be a last resort, strains the proportionality calculus, and violates the chivalric justice of treating an equal as an equal (via Paul Kahn's paradox of riskless warfare and Robert Sparrow's threat-based immunity). His proposal is that highly asymmetric force be applied with restraint, more like international policing than war.

samples.book: 079 - Frankenstein and Philosophy - The Shocking Truth
samples.title: Frankenstein and Philosophy
samples.relation: Galliott treats Frankenstein as the template for blaming lethal autonomous robots: Victor alone created his creature, but today's 'frankennovation' - Ronald Arkin's 'ethical governor' algorithms, DARPA funding, degree programs in robot warfare, and the South African robotic cannon that killed nine spectators - distributes responsibility across engineers, educators (Victor's father and Professors Krempe and Waldman, who never properly warned him about Agrippa's 'sad trash'), universities, and the military-industrial complex. Yet Shelley's articulate, Paradise Lost-quoting monster is a rational, intentional killer who can be held morally responsible and even punished, as Rob Sparrow demands of machines. Because responsibility does not dilute with numbers - two murderers do not get half a life sentence each - the chapter concludes that everyone in the chain, and all of us who do nothing to stop it, shares the blame for monstrous creations.

samples.book: 142 - The Avengers and Philosophy - Earth's Mightiest Thinkers
samples.title: “This is the Kind of Thing that is Going to Bite US in the Butt”
samples.relation: Melançon pictures Avengers ethics as Hawkeye's arrow sliding along a line from deontological duty toward consequentialist results, focusing on secrets and lies: Doctor Strange's deception—disguising his Sanctum Sanctorum as a coffee shop to shelter the underground New Avengers after Civil War—is tested against Michael Walzer's 'supreme emergency', the wartime exception (Allied bombing of Germany, the ticking time bomb) that permits violating your own values so they can survive. Strange keeps sliding—possessed by a demon against the Hulk—until the Eye of Agamotto strips him of his title, showing emergencies must stay rare and the agent 'worthy of surviving'. Steve Rogers's secret black-ops Secret Avengers repeat the danger: unlike democratic intelligence agencies, they have zero oversight or accountability, so the WikiLeaks-style leak of their informant dealings threatens the reputation of the whole Avengers enterprise.

name: Judgment of Taste and the Sublime

samples.book: 038 - Radiohead and Philosophy - Fitter Happier More Deductive
samples.title: 2. - Radiohead, or the Philosophy of Pop
samples.relation: Greif asks how pop music could ever 'incarnate a particular historical situation' and answers with Radiohead's portrait of broadcast culture around 2000: an environing, objectless dread in which each person lives at a knot of shouted messages no one sent and complaining only marks you as a crank. The band's turn to electronica was not avant-garde innovation but the discovery of the sound of that second nature, with Yorke's sampled-and-broken voice alternately absorbed into the machine and reasserting the human, and the lyric 'we' sliding between a scared individual lying that he is not alone, a wished-for collectivity, and the ventriloquized tyrant (as with Brecht's Pirate Jenny). Radiohead's church-tinged sublimity observes the storm from inside it — an internalized, inhuman sublime rather than the tradition's safe vantage on crushing power. Pop, he concludes, neither mirrors us nor preaches: it lets us retain and reactivate knowledge social speech forbids, and its deepest effect is not revolution but defiance — the retention of a private voice, a politics of re-created privacy — epitomized by 'There There' warning 'just 'cause you feel it doesn't mean it's there' inside an art form devoted to making you feel.

samples.book: 051 - Soccer and Philosophy - Beautiful Thoughts on the Beautiful Game
samples.title: VHS, DVD, YouTube
samples.relation: Vargiu seats Kant in the Maracanã grandstand (after the Monty Python philosopher match) to test aesthetic disinterest against football: the judgment of taste is 'merely contemplative' and indifferent to the object's existence—explained through Gadamer's reading of the third Critique—so the gambler, the torcida chanting 'we won', the ultras, and the players themselves (whose attention and struggle preclude contemplation) all fail the test, and Kant stands alone except for the neutral spectator and the Panofsky-style purist. Kant's free versus accessory beauty explains why knowing the offside rule adds an intellectual liking to the aesthetic one (Denilson's inconclusive samba dribbles versus Garrincha's effective ones), and the second feature of taste, general validity—saying 'that Maradona goal is the most beautiful ever' claims everyone's agreement without objective rules—underwrites FIFA's Goal of the Century polls and connects the third Critique to public, communicative reason. Finally, the rewatched match on VHS, DVD, or YouTube, where the result is already known and no bets can be laid, is where fans most often approach genuine disinterested contemplation of the object's mere image.

samples.book: 030 - Pink Floyd and Philosophy - Careful with that Axiom, Eugene!
samples.title: To Join in with the Game
samples.relation: Gracyk argues Waters is wrong that Pink Floyd ended when he quit in 1985: Waters's case rests on an illicit use of the identity of indiscernibles, since if losing Waters's lyrics destroys the band's identity, then losing Barrett's or Wright's, or adding 'Lucifer Sam,' would too, which proves too much. Borrowing Locke's distinction between the same man and the same person (the oak that remains the same oak through change; the unrecognized Syd in Abbey Road's Studio Three) and Kant's contrast between free and dependent beauty to explain how intentions change aesthetic evaluation, he defends actual intentionalism over hypothetical intentionalism: Hendrix really sings 'kiss the sky,' and interviews with Waters genuinely aid interpretation of Wish You Were Here. He then argues for collective agency, that groups can have intentions through members charged to act responsibly on the group's behalf, so no single member can disband a collective: Waters had a duty to leave, Gilmour, Mason, and Wright were entitled to continue the group's longstanding intention of making and performing original music, and the Echoes compilation is therefore an accurate portrait of the real Pink Floyd.

samples.book: 069 - Curb Your Enthusiasm and Philosophy - Awaken the Social Assassin Within
samples.title: Curb Your Enthusiasm and Philosophy
samples.relation: Takes the show's title as a literal ethical command and asks which senses of enthusiasm should be curbed, tracing the concept's history: Plato's muse-inspired poet in the Ion and Apology, the early Christian Enthusiasts, Wesley and Shaftesbury's attempts to separate good from bad enthusiasm, and the Enlightenment ridicule of Locke and Hume, for whom enthusiasm meant fanaticism, a pretended insight into the supernatural that Larry is right to mock. Kant gets the most sustained treatment: enthusiasts of friendship, religion, or patriotism inflame a good principle beyond its proper degree, which explains Larry's failure as a friend, while 'aesthetic enthusiasm,' the sublime 'idea of good with affect' before the morally good, is valuable, and Larry's single moment of it comes when the Arizona preacher's sermon on moral goodness sends him flying back to Los Angeles to donate his kidney to Richard Lewis. The verdict: curb fanatic and inauthentic enthusiasm (Ted Danson's everything-is-heaven), keep ordinary resoluteness and aesthetic enthusiasm, and accept that a society needs a few Larrys, the Socratic fools who yell for society.

samples.book: 159 - The Expanse and Philosophy - So Far Out Into the Darkness
samples.title: Howl at the Moon If You Want To
samples.relation: Michael J. O'Neill argues that infinite space is The Expanse's most constant on-screen character, conveyed through chiaroscuro cinematography that deliberately echoes the seventeenth century (the Don Quixote references, 'Dulcinea', the Rocinante's name), when humanity first confronted infinite space. He reads Pascal's terror at man as 'a middle point between all and nothing' into Avasarala's losing debate with Nancy Gao over the Ring gold rush and into Miller's agoraphobic quest for Julie, then contrasts this with Kant's mathematically and dynamically sublime: spacewalks, the Behemoth dwarfed at the Gate, the Arboghast disassembled over Venus, and Inaros' asteroid attack as the weaponization of the infinite. Against Pascal's insignificance, Kant's sublime reveals our freedom — Holden's 'crazy notion about free will' while descending to the Ring station, Drummer's 'nothing in the void is foreign to us', and Amos' 'we're still here' — so the awe the show's visuals provoke is an intuition that we are greater than all nature's power.

samples.book: 129 - RuPaul's Drag Race and Philosophy - Sissy That Thought
samples.title: 7. The Sublime Sabotage of the Inner Saboteur
samples.relation: Ryan reads Drag Race ontologically through Kant's two forms of the sublime from the Critique of Judgment: the spinning-prop disaster challenge in 'RuPocalypse Now', where queens like Jiggly Caliente are overwhelmed and then rise ('I couldn't let my fall be the death of me'), embodies the mathematically sublime, while Violet Chachki's sixteen-inch corset cinch and oxygen tank on the 'Death Becomes Her' runway dramatizes the dynamically sublime, the recognition of a power in us greater than what threatens us. She argues the queens' testimonies — Chi Chi on growing up poor, black and queer in the Deep South, Kim Chi's fear of her mother, Katya's confessed terror of failure — show free will and authenticity overcoming the determinism of normative structures of gender, race and class. The 'inner saboteur' is overcome through sublime self-overcoming and the solidarity of werkroom heart-to-hearts, even within a capitalist reality-TV machine she checks against the Paris Is Burning appropriation critique.

samples.book: 044 - Led Zeppelin and Philosophy - All Will Be Revealed
samples.title: Authentic Rock
samples.relation: Theodore Gracyk asks whether Zeppelin's uncredited borrowings—Willie Dixon's 'You Need Love' into 'Whole Lotta Love', Spirit's 'Taurus' into 'Stairway to Heaven', Jake Holmes's 'I'm Confused' into 'Dazed and Confused'—undermine their status as an authentic rock band whose value supposedly rests on sincere self-expression and original songwriting. Using Hanslick's thought experiment as staged by Little Roger and the Goosebumps's 'Gilligan's Island (Stairway)' parody and Handel's recycling of his own music into the Messiah, he argues a song's expressive power comes from the interaction of words and music (guarding against the fallacies of division and composition), and that by itself music is neither angry nor spiritual. Since Zeppelin's instrumental arrangements diverge radically from their sources and the lawsuits turned on Plant's lyrics, the chapter concludes that transformation, not narrow originality, grounds their genius—so the rock-versus-pop authenticity standard must be loosened.

samples.book: 010 - Mel Gibson's Passion and Philosophy - The Cross, the Questions, the Controversy
samples.title: Mel Gibson’s Passion and Philosophy
samples.relation: Irwin defends the film's violence aesthetically: beauty (Michelangelo's Pietà) distracts from moral truth rather than serving it, and Aristotle's Poetics fits the film neither as tragedy (a flawless Christ cannot fall through hamartia, and a good man's fall from prosperity is 'repulsive', so no catharsis explains why we watch) nor as the Plato-banned spectacle that inflames the passions, since it leaves viewers numb rather than belligerent. Instead he applies Cynthia Freeland's four features of the cinematic sublime, drawn from Burke and Kant: the flogging scenes, the grotesque Satan clutching his deformed child, Judas harried by demon-children to suicide, and even the Aramaic and Latin subtitles produce the pain-pleasure conflict, overwhelming vastness, and jolt from feeling to moral reflection that make the experience sublime. The violence is thus justified as Gibson's deliberate delivery of the sublime, provided viewers leave fear at the gates.

samples.book: 039 - Jimmy Buffett and Philosophy - The Porpoise Driven Life
samples.title: Wonder Why We Ever Go Home
samples.relation: Duke Richey maps Buffett's West — 'Ringling, Ringling,' the Rancho Deluxe soundtrack, Tully Mars — onto Josiah Royce's philosophy of community: only people who root in a place, face its history ('wise provincialism'), and sacrifice selfish desires for the whole can build Beloved Communities, a lesson enacted when cattle rustlers Jack and Cecil accept community sanction and find belonging working the Rancho Deluxe. Wallace Stegner's coral-reef metaphor from Angle of Repose supplies the image of communities built up millimeter by millimeter yet still vulnerable to pollution and over-fishing, with Royce's environmental regret (covering 'the wounds' of the landscape with gardens) anticipating the chapter's sustainability ethic. 'Wonder Why We Ever Go Home' thus asks what we really seek when we seek grace through community: not the nomadic Pickup Truck Death of every-man-for-himself, but cooperation that makes a society to match the scenery.

samples.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
samples.title: 34. The Lord of the Rings as Philosophy Environmental Enchantment and Resistance in Peter Jackson and J.R.R. T
samples.relation: Whitmire and Henderson read Peter Jackson's LotR films as environmental philosophy, arguing they use fantasy to recover a sense of nature's wonder and model a plurality of caring, non-instrumentalizing ways of inhabiting the land (Hobbits' gardens, the Rohirrim and their horses, the Elves of Lorien, the Ents of Fangorn) against the extractive, insatiable devastation of Saruman's Isengard and Sauron's Mordor. They explicitly deploy Leopold's Land Ethic ('the conqueror role is eventually self-defeating') to condemn Saruman's clear-cutting and dam-building, and Val Plumwood's ecofeminist notion of 'backgrounding' to explain why holding trees and mountains in visual focus is itself an argument. Thoreau's Maine Woods passage on the living pine grounds their claim that a tree is more than lumber, and the film's resistance (the Ents tearing out the dam, the White Tree's bloom) is read as a call to active ecological hope.

samples.book: 012 - Star Wars and Philosophy - More Powerful than You Can Possibly Imagine
samples.title: Restoring Balance to the Force
