samples.relation: Cooke uncovers an environmental ethic in Star Wars: after surveying anthropocentric resource-management views and Singer's anti-speciesism (Luke blithely shooting womprats, the Geonosian arena's abused beasts), she builds the chapter on Holmes Rolston III's claims that organisms and ecosystems have intrinsic value and that value is systemic and holistic. The 'living Force' - life creates it, midi-chlorians live symbiotically in all cells - makes Jedi training a discipline of respecting nature, exemplified by Yoda's mud hut on Dagobah and the self-sufficient Gungan and Ewok eco-communities that defeat droid armies and stormtroopers. Restoring balance to the Force therefore means restoring symbiotic balance between human culture and the natural world, which the chapter links to Leopold-style land-ethic holism of the biotic community.

samples.book: 202 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Shotgun. Machete. Reason
samples.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
samples.relation: Hinzmann and Arp ask whether walkers can be morally harmed, ranking perceptual, reasoning, and conscious minds and placing zombies at shark level on the evidence of Dr. Jenner's fMRI ('TS-19') showing only the brain stem reactivates. Surveying anthropocentric views (Michonne's chained pet-walkers as guard-dog tools), Singer's expanding circle, Leopold's land ethic, and Naess's deep ecology, they conclude that even utilitarians could demand a zombie preserve on the model of Hershel's barn of 'sick people', which Shane's barn massacre in 'Pretty Much Dead Already' destroys. Kant's point that cruelty to animals corrodes our humanity explains why the Governor's death-match arena, his torture of Rick and Michonne, and his chained zombie daughter mark him, not the walkers, as the true moral monster.

samples.book: 082 - Jurassic Park and Philosophy - The Truth Is Terrifying
samples.title: Jurassic Park and Philosophy
samples.relation: Fitzpatrick argues that the awe Ellie feels at the brachiosaurs makes experiencing real dinosaurs so valuable that restoring them may be obligatory, and reads Malcolm's distrust of land managers as sharing Leopold's land ethic, under which firebombing Isla Nublar would be barbarism on the order of Dresden. Invoking Bentham, Mill, and Singer's expansion of the moral community (echoed in the park's dart guns), he weighs Elliot's 'Faking Nature' and Katz's charge that restored nature is a fake and an arrogance against Andrew Light's defense of respectful restoration. He concludes that Jurassic Park failed not because restoration is wrong but because Hammond restored dinosaurs for amusement, and that a careful, land-ethic-respecting de-extinction could one day be justified.

samples.book: 068 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Zombie Apocalypse Now
samples.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
samples.relation: Hinzmann and Arp ask whether zombies can be morally harmed: Jenner's fMRI in 'TS-19' shows only the brain stem reactivates, leaving walkers with a merely shark-like 'perceptual mind.' Against anthropocentric theories, under which Michonne may keep her chained pet walkers as guard-dog tools, they set Singer's utilitarian expanding circle, Leopold's land ethic, and Naess's deep ecology, each of which could support a 'PETZ' zombie preserve. Hershel's barn of 'sick people' and Shane's massacre of it in 'Pretty Much Dead Already' show how fragile such preservation is, while the Governor's death-match arena ringed with chained zombies and his kept zombie daughter illustrate Kant's point that cruelty toward mere animals corrodes the humanity of the cruel person himself.

samples.book: 153 - Disney and Philosophy - Truth, Trust, and a Little Bit of Pixie Dust
samples.title: Intergenerational Ships and Sustainable Duties
samples.relation: Hackett uses WALL-E's lone plant and the Buy n Large Axiom to ask what we owe nature and future generations: WALL-E's tender care of the seedling models treating nature as a rights-bearing 'person' (via Gaia-superorganism thinking), while BnL's obese, screen-hooked passengers on the Axiom satirize capitalist individualism that acknowledges no obligations beyond contracts. He proposes a 'Principle of Sustainable Duties' — minimize net environmental damage and weigh long-term impact — and reads the film's open ending, extending Leopold's expansion of moral community to the biotic whole, as a Platonic aporia about whether an Anthropocene humanity can actually change in time.

samples.book: 275 - Hunting – Philosophy for Everyone - In Search of the Wild Life
samples.title: Hunting Philosophy for Everyone
samples.relation: Marvin, a social anthropologist, argues that for 'nature hunters' (Kellert's typology) a taxidermy trophy is not a dead animal but a living souvenir — un recuerdo — that enshrines the memory of a fair-chase hunt. Using Susan Stewart on the souvenir's part/whole incompleteness and Appadurai on value as 'difficulty of acquisition,' he shows how the lethal shot, the pose-reversed photograph, and the taxidermist's craft convert a wild animal into a personal memento that only lives through the hunter's narrative. How the animal was killed (ethically, authentically) matters more than that it was killed; the trophy is the hunter's self-awarded token of ethical excellence.

samples.book: 066 - Neil Gaiman and Philosophy - Gods Gone Wild!
samples.title: Neil Gaiman and Philosophy
samples.relation: Richard Rosenbaum asks how Gaiman's gods, abstract concepts made flesh who live or die by human belief, could exist, starting from Plato's Forms (Odin as personified battle-wisdom, Media as media) and the Allegory of the Cave, which gives new meaning to a protagonist literally named Shadow. Finding Forms too independent to need believers, he upgrades the metaphysics with Leibniz's Monadology: if everything, bodies and ideas alike, is composed of perception-bearing monads, then shared beliefs can agglomerate, 'level up' into a soul, and become a living god walking around America. Chalmers's hard problem of consciousness, panprotopsychism, and the claim that information has interdependent physical and phenomenal aspects supply the final mechanism, so collective belief realized phenomenally must become physically embodied, in contrast to the dualism of Descartes that made mind-body interaction mysterious.

samples.book: 012 - Star Wars and Philosophy - More Powerful than You Can Possibly Imagine
samples.title: “May The Force Be with You”
samples.relation: Jones uses the Force's telekinesis (Luke's lightsaber flying to his hand, Yoda raising the X-wing) to probe the metaphysics of causation. Hume shows we never observe the necessary connection between cause and effect - only constant conjunction and habit - so Jedi mind-power is no more mysterious than gravity or magnetism; Leibniz's Monadology argues one substance cannot transfer properties to another, so 'how' any cause works is unintelligible; and Hume's problem of induction (will Tatooine's twin suns rise tomorrow? will Vader's officers always choke?) shows law-governed expectations cannot be non-circularly justified. Concurring with Russell that 'cause' is a relic, the chapter concludes the Force qualifies as a kind of cause precisely because our causal concept is too vague to exclude it - and plugs science fiction as a laboratory for sharpening concepts.

samples.book: 046 - Mr. Monk and Philosophy - The Curious Case of the Defective Detective
samples.title: Herr Leibniz Consoles Mr. Monk
samples.relation: Kavas distinguishes Monk's method from Holmes's modus ponens, Poirot's elimination, and Goren's profiling: Monk accepts only what completes a coherent total narrative, so 'Here's what happened' re-tells the order of the whole world, as in the chess-game solution of 'Mr. Monk and the Genius'. The chapter uses the Tractatus's world of contingent, logically independent facts to model Monk's picture-completion, then brings in Leibniz: the principle of sufficient reason, the best of all possible worlds, and preestablished harmony justify Monk's faith that even Trudy's death must have a reason. Monk emerges as a pessimistic Leibniz who takes the world to be the worst possible precisely because, since learning the bomb was meant for Trudy in 'Mr. Monk Goes to Jail', he cannot see any sufficient reason for her death ('Why her?').

samples.book: 221 - The Philosophy of Film Noir
samples.title: Ride the Pink Horse Money, Mischance, Murder, and the Monads of Film Noir
samples.relation: Silver reads Robert Montgomery's Ride the Pink Horse as a prototypically noir embodiment of Schopenhauer's The World as Will and Representation. The revenge-driven Gagin, like Hugo, is enslaved to money and will—'a man can do what he wants, but not want what he wants'—and takes the limits of his own field of vision for the limits of the world, blind to the monads and Platonic-cave shadows of fate around him. Against him stand Pancho's suffering kindness and the Indian girl Pila's selfless compassion, which Silver aligns with Schopenhauer's dictum that 'compassion is the basis of all morality' and his prizing of aesthetic transcendence. The carousel (tío vivo) and the burning of Zozobra, the god of bad luck, become symbols of will's pointless circular striving from which only sacrifice and art offer escape.

samples.book: 055 - Doctor Who and Philosophy - Bigger on the Inside
samples.title: The Odd Thought of Doctor Who
samples.relation: Maps Leibniz's monadology onto the Whoniverse: the Doctor's individual concept survives each regeneration as a thinking monad while its bodily monads are replaced, parallel Liz Shaws in 'Inferno' show incompossible predicates, and the Time Lords play Leibniz's God permitting minimal evil, which the Doctor accepts in refusing to avert the Daleks' creation in 'Genesis of the Daleks'. The dimensionally transcendental TARDIS illustrates the principle of indiscernibles, the Matrix becomes a failed pre-established harmony haunted by confused perceptions, and the Master hallucinates against the Doctor like Descartes's evil demon. The Valeyard is modeled as an incompossible world on Leibniz's Sextus Tarquinius pyramid and Borges's forking paths, closing with Leibniz's own 'odd thought' academy of wonders.

samples.book: 244 - The Who and Philosophy
samples.title: The Odd Thought of Doctor Who
samples.relation: Gregory Kalyniuk maps Leibniz's monadology onto Doctor Who. The Doctor's identity across regenerations is a thinking monad whose individual concept holds necessary predicates while appurtenant body-monads are replaced; the Time Lords play Leibniz's God overseeing pre-established harmony and permitting evil in the best world (refusing to stop the Daleks in 'Genesis'). The dimensionally transcendental TARDIS illustrates the identity of indiscernibles, the Matrix is a Leibnizian mill of confused perceptions (with the Master as Descartes's evil demon), and the incompossible Valeyard of 'Trial of a Time Lord' is read via Leibniz's Theodicy pyramid and Borges's forking paths.

samples.book: 158 - Ender's Game and Philosophy - The Logic Gate Is Down
samples.title: Ender’s Game and Philosophy
samples.relation: Brett Patterson compares Card's philotes and the ansible to Leibniz's monadology — simple, internally varied building blocks whose twining connections mirror monadic 'intercommunication' at any distance — and reads the Giant's Drink landscape and the hive-queen pupa as the buggers' engineered face-to-face encounter with Ender. Through Levinas he argues the Other's ethical claim precedes self-knowledge, so the philotic bond installs a responsibility Ender cannot escape: he cannot go home because he must become Speaker for the Dead and restore the species he destroyed.

samples.book: 080 - Ender's Game and Philosophy - Genocide Is Child's Play
samples.title: Ender’s Game and Philosophy
samples.relation: Brett Patterson reads Card's philotes and the ansible as an uncanny parallel to Leibniz's Monadology - simple, internally varied, interconnected building blocks whose 'twining' explains instantaneous communication - and reads Ender's bond with the hive-queen through Levinas, for whom the face-to-face encounter with the Other imposes responsibility prior to self-understanding. That bond, formed through the Giant's Drink landscape the buggers built from Ender's own dreams, is why he cannot go home: he becomes Speaker for the Dead to restore the species he destroyed.

samples.book: 010 - Mel Gibson's Passion and Philosophy - The Cross, the Questions, the Controversy
samples.title: Mel Gibson’s Passion and Philosophy
samples.relation: Irwin takes Pilate's Quid est veritas as a guided tour of theories of truth applied to the film: Gibson's sympathetic Pilate embodies relativism, met with Nietzsche's 'truth is a woman' perspectivism and Baudrillard's postmodern laughter and rejected; Caiaphas and the bad thief demanding Jesus come down from the cross put the correspondence theory to work ('the proof is out there'), though beliefs hang on other beliefs ad infinitum; Simon of Cyrene's growing conviction models the coherence theory, exposed as necessary but not sufficient by Swinburne's case for versus Wells's case against the divinity of Jesus; and Pilate's Barabbas gambit parodies James's pragmatic theory, where working is not enough if there is no corresponding reality. He then retrieves Heidegger's reading of aletheia as uncovering, helped by the Quid est veritas anagram ('Est qui vir adest': it is the man before you) and Gadamer on truth seizing us like beauty, so that Jesus's 'I am the truth' and Claudia's dream-guided warnings point to truth as disclosure. Since disclosure alone cannot decide between inconsistent revealed claims, Irwin ends by leaving the viewer with a leap of faith and a first instinct as final answer.

samples.book: 129 - RuPaul's Drag Race and Philosophy - Sissy That Thought
samples.title: 11. Lip Sync for Your Life
samples.relation: Guilel Treiber reads the Season Ten reunion blow-up - Asia O'Hara blaming the show for letting The Vixen walk out, RuPaul insisting people must 'want to meet halfway' - as an unresolvable conflict between two value systems. The show's official 'C.U.N.T.' virtues (charisma, uniqueness, nerve, talent) are individualistic, market-driven values that professionalize drag, while the implicit 'A.S.S.E.' values (acceptance, solidarity, support, empowerment) descend from LGBTQ+ history from Stonewall and Marsha P. Johnson to ACT-UP. Using Nietzsche's On the Genealogy of Morals and its project of the 'revaluation of all values,' he argues values gain worth through conflict rather than progress, so there is no view from nowhere that settles the dispute. Miss Congeniality, the queens' revolt over Valentina's title, and Tammie Brown's clash with RuPaul show the show's magic lies in never deciding between the two - even though market pressure keeps devaluing solidarity.

samples.book: 173 - Inception and Philosophy - Because It's Never Just a Dream
samples.title: Leap of Faith
samples.relation: Dionne reads Cobb's 'idea is the most resilient parasite' as a claim about narrative: what gets incepted in Fischer is a story ('my father doesn't want me to follow in his footsteps'), and by the same token each of us is a collection of incepted stories rather than a stable self. Drawing on Bergson's account of perception mediated by memory and desire (Cobb's bridge triggering Mal's projection), Nietzsche's perspectivism — truth is a 'moral prejudice' and 'we must mistake ourselves' — and the embodiment of the being-in-the-world, she argues dreams differ from reality only in degree, since both are interested story-making under time pressure. The payoff is meta-filmic: Fischer is the spectator and Cobb the director, and the final spinning top becomes the audience's own totem — there is no fact of the matter, only interpretation, so watching the ending is itself the leap of faith.

samples.book: 012 - Star Wars and Philosophy - More Powerful than You Can Possibly Imagine
samples.title: “Trust Your Feelings”
samples.relation: Fader tackles the paradox that Jedi lie while Sith tell the truth: Obi-Wan's 'Darth Vader betrayed and murdered your father,' Yoda's trickster masquerade on Dagobah, the Council's cover-up of its waning powers, against Vader's brutal truth at Cloud City and Palpatine's technically honest 'I love democracy.' Kant's absolute prohibition of lying is set against the utilitarian's greatest-good lie and Nietzsche's claim that truth is the accepted set of social lies; Obi-Wan's deception is then defended through Plato's noble lie and the Buddha's Parable of the House on Fire, where 'expedients' to save the oblivious are no falsehood, while Vader and Dooku wield literal truths as weapons without compassion. Luke's answer is to stop accepting anyone's version and build his own green lightsaber: truth as perspective, intention, and finally the heart's understanding that redeems Anakin.

samples.book: 014 - The Atkins Diet and Philosophy - Chewing the Fat with Kant and Nietzsche
samples.title: The Atkins Diet and Philosophy
samples.relation: Bamford argues that Atkins's insistence that dieters evaluate the plan for their individual needs parallels Nietzsche's cultural therapy: as the death of God left modern culture nihilistic, so a processed-food culture suffers 'nutritional nihilism,' and the 'mega-orthodox' doctors who worship medical consensus with 'religious fervor' treat science as a replacement religion. Reading Ecce Homo's 'question of nutriment' alongside Twilight of the Idols, she shows that Nietzsche's perspectivism — no uninterpreted facts, only interpretations from physiological perspectives — makes each dieter fully responsible for interpretation, which is why Atkins must ask us to think for ourselves. The limit: where Atkins keeps an 'absolute faith in empirical science' (and Atkins Nutritionals mass-markets processed low-carb products), a properly Nietzschean therapy would question that faith too.

samples.book: 116 - 1984 and Philosophy - Is Resistance Futile
samples.title: 22. The Irrelevance of Truth
samples.relation: Jan Kyrre Berg Friis argues, with Nietzsche, that truth is a 'mobile army of metaphors', a relational event between people rather than an objective correspondence, and that the will to truth is subordinate to the will to power — the difference being that Trump-style 'alternative truth' is dishonest domination while Nietzsche's askesis is self-transformation. He layers in the Buddhist and Zen (Dogen) diagnosis of perception as conceptual distortion, Descartes' ego cogito as the fatal Western turn, and Heidegger's warning that calculative, technological thinking covers over our tacit lived background, producing exactly the one-dimensional minds a Ministry of Truth can feed. Rorty's advice to drop the truth-talk, Kant's insight that reality is sifted through the perceiver, and the cognitive-science of confirmation bias explain why facts no longer bite in the post-truth newsfeed.

samples.book: 062 - Inception and Philosophy - Ideas to Die For
samples.title: Leap of Faith
samples.relation: Dionne argues Cobb's 'most resilient parasite' works only as an idea embedded in a coherent story - 'my father doesn't want me to be him' - and that since ideas define who we are, each person is less a host than a collection of well-planted narratives. Using Bergson on embodied, memory-and-desire-mediated perception (Cobb's fear of the bridge triggering Mal's projection) and Nietzsche's Beyond Good and Evil on perspectival appearance as the price of life, she claims dreams differ from reality in degree, not kind: we are beings-in-the-world who stabilize contingency through story-making and 'strive for positive logic'. Hence knowledge always demands the leap of faith that Saito and Mal demand of Cobb, the film becomes a meta-narrative with Fischer as its audience, and the wobbling top offers only an interpretation of a fact, never the fact itself.

samples.book: 024 - Bullshit and Philosophy - Guaranteed to Get Perfect Results Every Time
samples.title: Rhetoric and Bullshit
samples.relation: Following Jeremy Campbell's The Liar's Tale, the chapter argues that the truth/lies binary is oversimplified: even 'the sky is blue' depends on contested definitions and 'God is good' on the speaker's concepts, so we must separate capital-T Truth — the immutable, incorruptible kind Plato located beyond the flawed physical realm of perfect Forms, which made him scorn rhetoric and the Sophists as teachers of disguise — from lower-case, situated, perspectival truths. It then recruits Nietzsche, for whom humans have no 'organ' for Truth but a natural instinct for falsehood (shared with camouflaging animals), and Ken Gemes's reading of doctrinal Truth as a ritualized fiction manufactured to maintain institutional and religious power. On this view postmodernism studies truth within the shifting domain of language rather than denying objective reality.

samples.book: 093 - More Doctor Who and Philosophy - Regeneration Time
samples.title: 15. The Way of the Doctor Is Deception
samples.relation: Dodge takes Rule #1 - the Doctor lies - through the major theories of lying: Bernard Williams's definition (asserting what you believe false with intent to deceive), Aristotle's claim that all lies are base, Kant's categorical imperative and respect for persons (even the Vinvocci's shimmer disguises in 'The End of Time' abuse trust), and Bentham's pleasure-pain calculus, which condemns the faked death at Lake Silencio ('The Impossible Astronaut') for the grief it caused Amy and Rory yet rewards the greater happiness it made possible. Against the absolutists he sets Plato's Noble Lie from the Republic - the elite falsehood that keeps society functioning - as what the Doctor emulates by deceiving the universe into thinking him dead ('The Wedding of River Song'), and Nietzsche's point in Human, All Too Human that lying is ethically neutral when the pretense is sustainable, as when the Doctor hides the ganger-Amy switch from Rory ('The Almost People'). The upshot: the Doctor's lies are wrong in themselves but routinely justified by the good they do, which is why sometimes the hero lies.

samples.book: 104 - Red Rising and Philosophy - Break the Chains!
samples.title: 10. Virtue Rising
samples.relation: Darci Doll argues the Rising exposes the Society's intellectual oppression—each Color denied education and fed 'noble lies' about its role—and that lifting it sparks an 'Intellectual Reformation' proving Color does not dictate potential: Darrow out-performing Golds, Orion the un-carved Blue, Ragnar and Sefi exceeding their station. She uses Plato's Republic (producers, auxiliaries, guardians, the lower orders kept obedient by Noble Lies like the Reds' terraforming myth) as the Society's blueprint, then turns to Aristotle: potential is realized only through the right environment, instruction, and habituated character, and Darrow's practical wisdom—testing himself, reassessing after Titus and Cassius, doing what makes him his best self—lets him flourish and lead. Aristotle's critique of utility-only relations explains why the Society's alliances expire (Antonia executed once useless) while Darrow and Mustang's virtue friendships and just rule endure, opening a society where everyone, including women and lowColors denied opportunity rather than ability, can maximize potential.

samples.book: 074 - Planet of the Apes and Philosophy - Great Apes Think Alike
samples.title: Planet of the Apes and Philosophy
samples.relation: Greg Littmann maps Ape City onto Plato's Republic class by class: orangutan rulers who legislate, censor, and propagandize; gorilla warriors who enforce; chimpanzee producers who do all the work - including, pointedly, the science Plato made no provision for; and humans as the 'barbarians' Plato says may be enslaved or exterminated. The overlaps are detailed: the Sacred Scrolls' first article of faith functions as the noble lie's myth of the metals, orangutan funerals promise heaven to keep gorillas unafraid of death, and Zaius's erasing of Taylor's dust-writing and blowing up of the archaeological cave enact the rulers' duty to supervise stories. But the films also refute Plato: hereditary orangutans show that power corrupts philosopher kings, Dr. Honorius's 'reason' is dogma serving the faith, the gelding threat that finally breaks Taylor cracks the tripartite-soul analogy of justice, and democracy's rough virtue is that it lets us remove rulers 'without sticking anybody with iron spears.'

samples.book: 094 - Divergent and Philosophy - The Factions of Life
samples.title: 8. Plato’s Chicago
samples.relation: Littmann systematically maps Roth's Chicago onto Plato's Republic: like Marcus, Plato rejects democracy after Athens executed Socrates; both dissolve the family ('faction before blood' versus children raised in common and bred by state schedule); Erudite's IQ-selected leadership mirrors the rigorously trained philosopher-rulers, Dauntless the warrior class whose purely physical training Plato warns turns 'savage and harsh,' Abnegation's poverty the guardians's communism of property, and the factionless the powerless producers - with Plato's noble lie about the metals matching the Erudite's propaganda and serums as instruments of control. The shared flaw, he argues, is concentrated power without external checks, which corrupted Abnegation, corrupts every Dauntless leadership change, and would corrupt Plato's guardians too. The lesson is not to hand power to the least vicious but for democratic voters to confront their own ignorance - or end like Roth's America, in apocalyptic war.

samples.book: 184 - The Office and Philosophy - Scenes from the Unexamined Life
samples.title: The Office and Philosophy
samples.relation: Tests the deceptions swirling around Dwight: Kant's two arguments against lying (universalizing the maxim 'lie whenever it saves face', and treating the deceived as a mere means) are set against Plato's noble lie from the Republic - Michael's empty 'Assistant Regional Manager' title may be a morally tolerable verbal lie because after 'The Fight' it restores their friendship, though it does not medicate the office as Plato's lie does the city. Epicurus' claim that only what is experienced can harm you ('what you don't know can't hurt you') is refuted by the thought of Angela's hypothetical fake love for Dwight: undetected deception is itself a harm. Finally Dwight's self-deception (believing the false promotion, Jim's telekinesis prank, the fax from his future self) is modeled by dividing the self - Plato's tripartite soul versus Descartes' simple, indivisible mind - suggesting cognitive science's modular brain as the better picture, and asking whether one can even wrong oneself.

samples.book: 157 - Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy - Read and Gain Advantage on All Wisdom Checks
samples.title: Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy
samples.relation: Cooke defends his three-year campaign of a lawful evil wizard (Oraximon, who magic-missiled an innkeeper and hid the bodies in a rope trick) against religious and secular critics. The epistemic charge fails because rulebooks are invitations to imagine, not assertions, and the Smurfs-as-Krishna example shows an 'attitude for export' needs authorial evidence D&D lacks; Hume's twin claims about the impropriety of imaginatively endorsing flawed sentiments are dismantled by splitting Can'tians from Won'tians over Gendler's stories and defending a 'Hardian' view on which resistance is just difficulty, making imaginative resistance a chimera. The causal charge fails on the evidence (the Werther effect and its video-game and jazz cousins are post hoc plus confirmation bias), the character-warping charge risks the unfalsifiability of the repressed-desire diagnosis, and Plato's ban on the arts — enforced via the noble lie — would be the price if imagining were as bad as doing.

samples.book: 018 - Harley-Davidson and Philosophy - Full-Throttle Aristotle
samples.title: Harley-Davidson and Philosophy
samples.relation: Rollin opposes mandatory helmet laws by contrasting two conceptions of freedom: the Hobbesian absence-of-constraint view ('go to hell in my own way', from Pinocchio's 'no strings on me' to the trapped coyote) and the rational-order view running from Plato (ranked classes, noble lies, censorship, contempt for democracy) through Rousseau's 'forced to be free', which Popper already identified as the enemy of the open society. Since, as the obesity-as-disease example and Robert Paul Wolff's expert-government argument show, we cannot claim certainty about value judgments the way we can about fractures, paternalism fails: if danger justified coercion we would have to ban motorcycles, skiing, parachuting, and bull-riding alike. Helmet laws in effect claim society knows what you ought to want better than you do, and Rollin's answer to his British colleague's 'what will you do if you injure your brain?' is to join the Department of Food Science and Nutrition.

samples.book: 145 - The Big Bang Theory and Philosophy - Rock, Paper, Scissors, Aristotle, Locke
samples.title: The Big Bang Theory and Philosophy
samples.relation: Fallis uses Sheldon — a lousy liar with an elaborate theory of lying — to probe the philosophy of lying: Kant's absolute prohibition (even 'out of frivolity'), Bok's presumption against deceit, Plato's noble lies reserved for philosopher kings, and Nietzsche's self-deceiving overmen, whose counsel explains the 'un-unravelable webs' of fake Facebook and blog evidence for the imaginary cousin Leopold Houston. Ryle's knowing-how versus knowing-that split explains how Sheldon can state the rules ('casually, no rapid breathing') yet botch the performance, while the Bazinga! pranks and the insincere courtroom apology break the Augustinian definition that lying requires intent to deceive. Grice's norms of conversation then ground the author's own definition — lying as intending to violate the norm against saying what you believe false — until a hypothetical, convention-oblivious liar like Kripke forces him to concede a counterexample and admit he was wrong.

samples.book: 019 - Monty Python and Philosophy - Nudge Nudge, Think Think!
samples.title: The Epilogue A Question of Belief
samples.relation: Systematically pairs Hume's philosophy of religion with Python parodies: Anselm's ontological argument fails because existence cannot be defined into a concept (the Yeti-spotter who never spotted one), with Arthur 'Two Sheds' Jackson, Ron Obvious, and Confuse-A-Cat illustrating the gap between conceivability and possibility; the Galaxy Song's cosmic order and the mock hymn 'All Things Dull and Ugly' stage the design argument and Hume's reply that creation shows moral indifference as readily as benevolence; and Brian's 'miracles' — being 'taken up' then spotted sprinting, curing Simon the hermit by landing on his foot — illustrate Hume's 'Of Miracles' on the unreliability of testimony. Hume's Natural History claim that the cause of religion is fear surfaces in the 'O Father, please don't boil us' hymn and in Arthur's groveling before a God who hates it. Both Hume and the Pythons end in suspended judgment about God — settled, if at all, only by the wrestling match in which 'God exists by two falls to a submission.'

samples.book: 046 - Mr. Monk and Philosophy - The Curious Case of the Defective Detective
samples.title: Does the Habit Make the Monk
samples.relation: Elliott maps the recurring Monk stalemate onto medieval theology: in 'Mr. Monk Goes to the Circus', Stottlemeyer and Disher reason forward from a hunch and the evidence, exactly like Anselm's ontological argument, which assumes what it sets out to prove, while Monk, like Aquinas against Anselm, refuses assumptions and reasons backward from verifiable facts, asking why an assassin would somersault except to advertise the acrobatic alibi. Aquinas's First Cause argument (Aristotle's unmoved mover) supplies the model of proving a certainty from observable things, paralleling Monk's 'I don't know how he did it, but he did it' backward deduction. The chapter's closing move likens Monk to the medieval monks themselves: his OCD-driven ascetic withdrawal from the dirty, chaotic world (contemptus mundi) is what lets him notice the imperfection in scenes like the locker room of 'Mr. Monk and the Big Game' that reveals sabotage.

samples.book: 012 - Star Wars and Philosophy - More Powerful than You Can Possibly Imagine
samples.title: The Force Is with You . . . but You’re Not a Jedi Yet
samples.relation: The editors' introduction argues that beneath its action scenes Star Wars stages ageless philosophical questions through the Skywalkers' struggles with identity, truth, freedom, and tragedy, opening with 'I've got a bad feeling about this' as basic philosophical wonder and doubt. It playfully transposes classic problems onto the saga: an Euthyphro-style question of whether Jedi virtues are good because the Jedi appreciate them, Anselm's question whether Yoda is a master greater than which cannot be conceived, Augustine on whether Anakin can be chaste 'but just not yet,' Machiavelli on Palpatine's Empire, Descartes' mind-body question asked of C-3PO, Hume's problem of induction applied to whether the sun will rise on Alderaan, Nietzsche's abyss for Vader, and Sartre's hell for the Sith. It previews each contributor's chapter rather than settling any question, framing the volume as a Kessel Run for the brain.

samples.book: 213 - Tennis and Philosophy - What the Racket Is All About
samples.title: Why Roger Federer Is the Best Or Is It McEnroe
samples.relation: David Baggett asks who is the all-time best male tennis player and treats it as a genuine problem in metaphysics ('what is the case?') and epistemology ('how do we know it?'), surveying candidates from Tilden to Federer against ten criteria. He argues the sentence 'Federer is the all-time best' is vague, running the tennis-ball-losing-an-atom sorites through three theories of vagueness—fuzzy logic, supervaluationism, and Timothy Williamson's epistemicism, which he favors: there is a fact of the matter (God knows it) but our closeness-to-the-margin ignorance keeps us from knowing it. He uses Anselm's ontological argument and Guanilo's perfect-island reply to distinguish the all-time best from the best-possible player, and invokes Sartre's existentialist rejection of mere potentiality ('could've/should've') to insist he is asking who actually was best, not who might have been.

samples.book: 125 - Rick and Morty and Philosophy - In the Beginning Was the Squanch
samples.title: 4. Could a Divine Creator Turn Out to Be a Selfish Jerk
samples.relation: Using 'The Ricks Must Be Crazy', where Morty discovers Rick's car battery is a microverse of gooble-box workers ('slavery with extra steps'), the chapter asks whether a universe's designer must be a perfect God or could be a clever jerk like Rick. It lays out Paley's watchmaker teleological argument, Hume's point that even a real designer need not be morally perfect, the Euthyphro dilemma against Divine Command Theory (would Rick's commands for middle-finger greetings become morally good?), and Plantinga's modal ontological argument recast across the show's multiverse of possible worlds like the one where Hitler cured cancer. It concludes that Rick's advice to just not think about it is exactly what Socrates refused to do.

samples.book: 130 - The Good Place and Philosophy - Get an Afterlife
samples.title: 6. A Better Bad Place
samples.relation: Grosz asks whether Judge Gen could justly condemn Team Cockroach to eternal torment, testing the classic 'sins against an infinite being deserve infinite punishment' defense built on Anselm's God as that than which nothing greater can be conceived, and finding that no such being exists on the show. He rejects the continuing-sin model of Hell because the Bad Place's physical torture precludes both further sinning and moral reform, and argues purely retributive eternal punishment fails the utilitarian test. His proposal, a non-torturous 'Bad Place 3.0' modeled on C.S. Lewis's The Great Divorce where people face the natural consequences of their vice until they reform, could be justified as what is best for the person.

samples.book: 048 - The Red Sox and Philosophy - Green Monster Meditations
samples.title: What Makes the Red Sox Great Is More than the Team
samples.relation: Ulatowski argues the 'We Believe' motto is religious: Red Sox fandom is the a priori conviction that Boston is the sports city 'than which none greater can be conceived,' transplanting Anselm's ontological argument—necessary, contingent and impossible objects, existence as a perfection—to the Red Sox via Oliver Wendell Holmes's 'hub of the universe.' He rejects the parallel New York argument because it smuggles a posteriori championship counts into an a priori proof, and answers the fallacy-of-division worry by making Boston's greatness and the Red Sox's greatness an identity rather than a whole-to-part inference.

samples.book: 010 - Mel Gibson's Passion and Philosophy - The Cross, the Questions, the Controversy
samples.title: Mel Gibson’s Passion and Philosophy
samples.relation: Taliaferro, writing as a personalist, worries that Gibson's relentless focus on torture eclipses the whole person of Christ: like torture victims losing peripheral vision, viewers lose sight of his teaching, healings, nonviolence, and resurrection, and the satisfaction-theology framing risks relishing redemptive suffering itself. His reconciliation thought-experiment (Patricia's betrayal of Kris and the God-man who resurrects the murdered child) argues that the resurrection, not the passion alone, completes at-one-ment, since no amount of suffering can undo past wrong. He contrasts Gandalf's laughing return in The Return of the King with a Gibson Jesus who could not plausibly laugh after rising, and invokes Scheler's St. Francis, who loves the wholeness behind sickness rather than the sickness, to urge that the film's intensity edges out a life-affirming view of persons as irreducibly valuable in themselves.

samples.book: 178 - LEGO and Philosophy - Constructing Reality Brick by Brick
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: Mentyka uses minifigure puzzles — can 'Eliza' and 'Beth' be distinct characters when built from identical pieces, and is Eliza the same character after every piece is swapped out, a minifig Ship of Theseus — to introduce the philosophy of the human person. He runs through supervenience on physical parts, Locke's memory theory and its Butler–Reid controversy (Reid in the taxonomy), the Christian Resurrection-of-the-Body background, and Parfit's despairing deflation that identity matters less than what survives us. Against these he defends personalism, citing Max Scheler and Kierkegaard's call in The Single Individual to become one rather than a crowd: a person is both the sigfig and the AFOL building it, constituted by free choices and actions — which is also why the LEGO Movie's 'Where Are My Pants?' mass society is the enemy.

samples.book: 013 - Superheroes and Philosophy - Truth, Justice, and the Socratic Way
samples.title: Power and Glory Tests of Virtue
samples.relation: The chapter's thesis is that superhero ethics is not utilitarianism (whose perverse 'evil twin' governs Marvel villains) but personalism - the tradition from Borden Parker Bowne to Martin Buber, rooted in Kant's insistence that every person be treated as an end and never merely as a means, and aiming at his 'kingdom of ends'. Heroes who refuse to weigh one innocent against the many enact personalism, and it redeems even Galactus: lying defeated, he is saved by Captain America's and Reed Richards' insistence that 'We had no choice, Galactus', which wins the devourer into a moral community. The authors read the whole arc as the ancient warning against hubris retold in contemporary storytelling.

samples.book: 128 - Mister Rogers and Philosophy - Wondering through the Neighborhood
samples.title: 14. A Party to Celebrate the Personal
samples.relation: Eric Mohr reads the 'Everybody's Special' week, Prince Tuesday shedding his royal cape because 'It's what's inside you that makes you special,' the plate factory that discards irregular plates, and King Friday's sameness mask-edict undone by Lady Elaine, as Max Scheler's personalism: persons are unique, unrepeatable 'individual value-essences' whose value only love discloses, which is why Corney's birthday party matters. Against the Aristotelian view that the soul is one universal form and our bodies merely individuate us, Scheler and Rogers hold the inner self is where difference deepens.

samples.book: 157 - Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy - Read and Gain Advantage on All Wisdom Checks
samples.title: Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy
samples.relation: Morton argues that to play D&D well is to do phenomenology: mapping a dungeon enacts a Heideggerian 'worlding' in which players generate care and concern for the entities around them, and the smudged, blood-stained survivor's journal in The Lost Caverns of Tsojcanth — alluding to the dwarves' book in Moria — shows that worlds are never transparent but allure, drawing players in through mystery (Harman's 'allure'). Against Heidegger's remark that animals are 'poor in world' and Lacan and Žižek's claim that only humans stick out of their life-world, he borrows Harman's 'sincerity' (with Husserl's intentional objects) to say every entity is stuck inside its own incomparable world — Elvish sincerity, Orcish sincerity, the Illusionist whose spells are a recursive play of illusion inside a game of illusion. D&D thereby caps the history of realism: where the novel moved from letters to focalization under a controlling narrator, the RPG replaces the master narrator with 'willing disbelief', letting players handle Romantic story-worlds — Tolkien's Middle-earth template, Greyhawk's continents, the Astral Plane's many planes — as DIY totalities that can be punctured, sorted, and rebuilt at will.

samples.book: 046 - Mr. Monk and Philosophy - The Curious Case of the Defective Detective
samples.title: It’s a Gift ... and a Curse
samples.relation: Welsh argues Monk's 'gift and curse' is being permanently stuck in Husserl's phenomenological attitude. Selective-attention experiments (the swapped interviewer behind the door, the gorilla-suit walker) show that the rest of us see only what expectation renders possible, while Monk, like Poe's Dupin finding the Purloined Letter in plain sight, brackets his assumptions and actually perceives: the moved decorative rock in Dr. Kroger's courtyard, the wing-back chair and wiped bullets proving the 'suicide' in 'Mr. Monk and the Garbage Strike' is murder, and the illiterate suspect's English-sign slip in 'Mr. Monk Goes to a Fashion Show' — all through his hand-framing 'Zen Sherlock Holmes thing.' But because he cannot exit back into the natural attitude, the same perception is pathological. Drawing on Damasio's Descartes' Error and Merleau-Ponty's patient Schneider, the chapter argues that emotion is what structures relevance and action, so Monk's refusal to let emotional bonds organize his life leaves him isolated and unhappy — though curing the curse might cost him the gift that solves the cases.

samples.book: 173 - Inception and Philosophy - Because It's Never Just a Dream
samples.title: Guilt Can be a Real Bitch
samples.relation: Jason Howard argues Inception is phenomenological philosophy in Husserl's sense: the film dramatizes how dreaming, remembering, and perceiving are distinct intentional states with different 'modes of givenness' and horizons — time dilates, dreams begin mid-scene with no past, and memories carry a temporal signature that collapses when Cobb rebuilds them into dreamscapes, which is why he warns Ariadne never to build dreams from memory. Totems work because waking perception alone is governed by laws of nature and by the shared life-world (Lebenswelt): Saito's carpet with the wrong fabric, Cobb's backwards watch, and the Penrose steps that could never close real space all betray the dream. The chapter extends this to embodiment — Yusuf's dreamers register rain and balance from their bodies, and Saito's comatose body still atrophies — and closes with intersubjectivity: Cobb's guilt is 'always there reminding me of the truth' because reality is inseparable from the community of others, and the 'shades' of people in dreams and memories can never capture the real Mal or his children.

samples.book: 037 - The Wizard of Oz and Philosophy - Wicked Wisdom of the West
samples.title: Nightmares
samples.relation: Auxier asks why the flying monkeys and the shriveling feet of the Wicked Witch of the East give children lifelong nightmares, and answers with a phenomenology of three frightening sequences in escalating duration: the instant shriveling shot, the five-minute cyclone (paired with 'The Great Gig in the Sky' in the Dark Side of the Rainbow sync), and the monkey air-raid. Kierkegaard's Concept of Anxiety supplies the depth psychology: innocence is ignorance, and the child's dreaming spirit projects its own nothing outward, fastening fear onto figures like the monkeys (who are, he notes, played by the Munchkin actors themselves). Merleau-Ponty's lived body versus habit body explains the mechanics: cinema seizes the body's usual 'tour of inspection,' Fleming manipulates active and passive synthesis (the scoreless build-up to the window blow, the barely noticed arsenal of weapons in the Haunted Forest, the dimming lights), and children construct a rigid, inescapable habit body within a single viewing, so the nightmare is the monkey inside our own projected world.

samples.book: 021 - U2 and Philosophy - How to Decipher an Atomic Band
samples.title: U2 and Philosophy
samples.relation: Han-Pile tests three traditional philosophies of music against U2's own talk about music: the rationalist (Descartes and Leibniz's 'unconscious exercise of arithmetic', satirized by Hit Song Science finding U2 mathematically close to Beethoven), the subjectivist (Hegel and Wackenroder on music as the expression of inner feeling, mirrored in Bono's method of articulating in words the feeling the band first found in improvisation), and the metaphysical (the Pythagorean-Boethian musica mundana whose harmony with our music 'Gloria' and 'Wake Up Dead Man' both invoke, consummated in Schopenhauer's music as direct copy of the will, which Nietzsche's critique of Wagner undermines). Against all three she sets Heidegger's Stimmung: music discloses shared moods - atmospheres that color how a whole world shows up, as 'Beautiful Day' or 'Bullet the Blue Sky' demonstrate. U2's vocation is thus to shift the numbed basic disposition of the age ('Zooropa', 'Numb') toward joy and compassion - rock 'n' roll as an alarm clock for 'dreaming up the world we want to live in'.

samples.book: 030 - Pink Floyd and Philosophy - Careful with that Axiom, Eugene!
samples.title: The Sun Is Eclipsed by the Moon
samples.relation: Randall Auxier uses Sartre's Psychology of Imagination to explain what 'Brain Damage' and 'Eclipse' do to a listener: auditory images live in time (unlike the spatial visual image of the prism cover), so Waters's repeated 'The lunatic is on the grass' and the anticipated drum entrances seize the will through repetition and the vortex of attention, while musicians themselves escape through an expanded 'now' — the trap-door in time Gilmour knows too well. Sartre's four positional acts of the image (positing the object as non-existent, absent, existing elsewhere, or neutral) are then worked through examples: imaging the contingently absent song, the superstition around imagining a beloved as dead (mode 1), and the neutral mode (4) that Pink Floyd favors over both benevolent and malevolent negations. The dark conclusion: music like Metallica at Guantanamo cancels the will, but Pink Floyd uses neutrality to show that in annihilating the world you destroy above all yourself and remain responsible for the choice — the sun eclipsed by the moon.

samples.book: 038 - Radiohead and Philosophy - Fitter Happier More Deductive
samples.title: Where Pink Floyd Ends and Radiohead Begins
samples.relation: Reisch asks whether Radiohead is the Pink Floyd of the twenty-first century and answers that the comparison misleads: where Barrett-era Floyd used electronics to escape into psychedelic fantasy, Radiohead's apparent space-rock is phenomenological, giving voice to pre-reflective experience of technological modern life. He reads 'No Surprises' (Yorke singing with his head in a filling glass sphere) as a study in the political infantilization of commuters, and OK Computer's car crash ('Airbag'), 'Let Down', and 'Lucky' as registering the feel of a fragile, technology-saturated world. Quoting Marcuse's One-Dimensional Man and Chomsky on manufactured consent, he argues we can see no alternative to the technologically rational system, and then, against Descartes' priority of the isolated 'I', invokes Heidegger's Being-in-the-world and Merleau-Ponty's embodied subject to suggest that our deepening immersion in technology may be changing the self itself — the truth the collapsing pedestrians of the 'Just' video cannot face.

samples.book: 061 - Sherlock Holmes and Philosophy - The Footprints of a Gigantic Mind
samples.title: The Essence of Perception Holmes’s Intention and Objects Intended
samples.relation: Kilroy romanticizes not the drugs but the woodshed: Holmes's cocaine sessions, violin, and clattered study cultivate a Husserlian field of consciousness in which reality is the intercourse of subject and object, so a clue (the Trichinopoly cigar ash, 'Rache' as German for revenge) only appears to a detective whose knowledge, observation, and deduction are unified — Gregson and Lestrade misread the same room in A Study in Scarlet because they theorize before the evidence. Heidegger's distinction between merely present (Vorhandenheit) and usefully present (Zuhandenheit) objects explains what counts as a clue — the lipstick-stained wineglass, not the tablecloth — and Husserl's 'things seen are always more than what we really and actually see' explains the frozen-coaster chair. Watson's see-it-to-believe-it empiricism, drained by the Afghan war, is precisely why he has no 'special powers': he never furnishes his brain-attic with the furniture that lets objects speak.

samples.book: 010 - Mel Gibson's Passion and Philosophy - The Cross, the Questions, the Controversy
samples.title: Mel Gibson’s Passion and Philosophy
samples.relation: Irwin takes Pilate's Quid est veritas as a guided tour of theories of truth applied to the film: Gibson's sympathetic Pilate embodies relativism, met with Nietzsche's 'truth is a woman' perspectivism and Baudrillard's postmodern laughter and rejected; Caiaphas and the bad thief demanding Jesus come down from the cross put the correspondence theory to work ('the proof is out there'), though beliefs hang on other beliefs ad infinitum; Simon of Cyrene's growing conviction models the coherence theory, exposed as necessary but not sufficient by Swinburne's case for versus Wells's case against the divinity of Jesus; and Pilate's Barabbas gambit parodies James's pragmatic theory, where working is not enough if there is no corresponding reality. He then retrieves Heidegger's reading of aletheia as uncovering, helped by the Quid est veritas anagram ('Est qui vir adest': it is the man before you) and Gadamer on truth seizing us like beauty, so that Jesus's 'I am the truth' and Claudia's dream-guided warnings point to truth as disclosure. Since disclosure alone cannot decide between inconsistent revealed claims, Irwin ends by leaving the viewer with a leap of faith and a first instinct as final answer.

samples.book: 025 - The Beatles and Philosophy - Nothing You Can Think that Can't Be Thunk
samples.title: CHAPTER 4 “A REVELATION TO BEHOLD”
samples.relation: Argues that the Beatles' devotion to rock and roll was a literal religious phenomenon rather than loose metaphor: Lennon's first hearing of Elvis is analyzed as a William James-style conversion, the Radio Luxembourg broadcasts were treated 'like scripture,' Hamburg was a 'baptism by fire,' and Epstein's new suits at the Cavern were announced as 'a revelation.' Drawing on James's Varieties of Religious Experience and Pragmatism, the chapter reads Beatlemania's screaming crowds as collective ecstatic ritual and the 'toppermost of the poppermost' chant as the will-to-believe making its own truth, in the way James says truth 'happens' to an idea. Aristotle's four causes supply the metaphysical frame — the 'magic' of Liverpool and the sacred quality fans reported are formal-final causation against the material-efficient causation of disenchanted modernity — while the band's double irony ('tarrying with the negative,' after Hegel) let them hold skepticism inside belief, as in Lennon's 'flaming pie' origin parody and the 'more popular than Jesus' episode.

samples.book: 021 - U2 and Philosophy - How to Decipher an Atomic Band
samples.title: U2 and Philosophy
samples.relation: Cleveland sorts the knowing and feeling of U2's lyrics ('Vertigo', 'Beautiful Day', 'Staring at the Sun', 'Daddy's Gonna Pay for Your Crash Car') into Russell's varieties of knowledge - propositional, acquaintance, know-how - and argues that the feeling U2 champions against thought is knowledge by acquaintance: direct, concept-free awareness that, in religious cases, just is Jamesian mystical revelation as against revelation as a set of propositional truths, which is why Bono tells his father he 'hears something back from the silence' rather than holding doctrines. James supplies both the view that feeling is the deeper source of religion and the pragmatist answer to the problem of origins - 'by their fruits ye shall know them', so religious feeling is vindicated by moral transformation. Hume's slave-of-the-passions thesis explains why such feeling, not inert moral knowledge, moves Bono's social justice work: 'God is love, and as much as I respond... in acting in that love, that's my religion'.

samples.book: 066 - Neil Gaiman and Philosophy - Gods Gone Wild!
samples.title: Neil Gaiman and Philosophy
samples.relation: Ray Bossert reads American Gods as an allegory of American philosophy: like Gaiman's gods, American philosophers labor invisibly in the background while European publics canonize their thinkers, and Shadow's prison exchanges show the point, since Loki must beg him to read Herodotus ('It's cool') while Johnnie Larch's 'don't piss off people who work in airports' beats Shadow's abstract generalization in usefulness. Following Hickman's Deweyan instrumentalism, he argues the gods are survival tools humans craft from need and discard when obsolete, so Czernobog's hammer gives way to Media's television, Wednesday treats even his own son as an instrument, and the buffalo man's 'believe everything' is advice about keeping one's tools of survival working. The chapter ends on liberty: Shadow refuses to be a god because 'we don't need anyone to believe in us,' and in the Egyptian death trial he claims the most American reward, the freedom to choose his own afterlife.

samples.book: 037 - The Wizard of Oz and Philosophy - Wicked Wisdom of the West
samples.title: “Here, Here, What’s All This Jabber-wapping When There’s Work to Be Done ”
samples.relation: Tschaepe reads Professor Marvel and the Wizard as skilled givers of 'folk explanations'—stories about desires, beliefs, and feelings that work where logical, scientific, or mechanistic explanations fail—because each explanation is fitted to the pragmatic considerations of its audience and problem. With the companions the Wizard works through a failed dualist argument (a brain is not a mind) for the Scarecrow, an abbreviated Stoic ataraxy pitch for the Tin Man, and Aristotle's discretion-is-valor point for the Lion, settling in each case on folk psychology plus a token (Th.D. diploma, heart-shaped clock, Legion of Courage medal) that supplies the recognition actually needed. Dorothy, whose desire for home is real rather than mistaken, gets no folk explanation from anybody: she must combine the heel-tapping instruction with her own articulated desire—'there's no place like home'—which the chapter treats as pragmatically, not logically, effective.

samples.book: 279 - Christmas – Philosophy for Everyone - Better Than a Lump of Coal
samples.title: Christmas Philosophy for Everyone
samples.relation: Holt argues that Seinfeld's Festivus, invented by Frank Costanza as an anti-consumerist 'holiday for the rest of us,' is grounded in American pragmatism: truth is 'whatever works,' malleable and tested by results. Because commercialized Christmas fails to deliver the altruism it demands, it 'does not work' and by pragmatist standards ceases to be true, so Costanza pragmatically forges a holiday that fits his needs. Holt reads Festivus's elements pragmatically — the maintenance-free aluminum pole as a bare functional symbol, the airing of grievances as a needed cathartic release from everyday restraint, the wrestling as self-perpetuating ritual — and warns that as Festivus merchandise spreads it will lose its practicality and, being no longer pragmatic, be discarded; he closes with a mock 'airing of grievances' against philosophers including Plato and Bertrand Russell.

samples.book: 065 - Chuck Klosterman and Philosophy - The Real and the Cereal
samples.title: Chuck Klosterman and Philosophy
samples.relation: Vannatta reads Klosterman's born-again pop culture — the Left Behind novels, Victory TV's Steven, Kurt Warner's Super Bowl, Jesus Camp — as living Puritan Calvinism: original sin (Klosterman's cruel third-graders), justification by faith alone, unmediated access to God ('every man was his own priest'), and predestination that leaves uncertain whether our actions matter in the divine equation. The chapter's pivot is truth versus peace: Puritan-born-again certainty sacrifices peace for antecedent truth, from the 1675 Massachusetts settlements to Robertson and Falwell on 9/11. Against this Vannatta sets the pragmatist alternative — truth as the outcome of communal inquiry in service of peaceful living — recasting God as the web of relationships and dissolving his own childhood camp's contradiction between 'I'm Third' and its cult of competition.

samples.book: 012 - Star Wars and Philosophy - More Powerful than You Can Possibly Imagine
samples.title: “A New Hope”
samples.relation: Long stages William Clifford's ethics of belief against William James's will to believe, with Luke Skywalker as James's exemplar. Clifford's shipowner story condemns faith as 'wrong always, everywhere, and for anyone,' which would convict Luke of immorality when he switches off his targeting computer and trusts the Force; James replies that where a choice is intellectually undecidable and a genuine option - live, forced, and momentous, like Luke's turn to the Jedi life or Obi-Wan's response to Leia's hologram - pragmatic faith is justified and even salvific. Faith can create truths: Han flying into the asteroid field, Luke's unjustified belief that there is good in Vader bringing Anakin back, the author's faith in his students, and Martin Luther King Jr.'s dream - all illustrating 'a new hope.'

samples.book: 041 - Stephen Colbert and Philosophy - I Am Philosophy (And So Can You!)
samples.title: It-Getting The Truth about Truthiness
samples.relation: Ethan Mills runs a 'Better Know a Skeptic' four-parter applied to the show: Pyrrhonian skepticism (Sextus Empiricus's suspension of judgment and living by appearances, played out in the Jon-says-worst-versus-Stephen-says-greatest Bush debate), Modern skepticism (Montaigne's fideist custom-worship and Hume's dream argument for why knowledge of couches, Doritos, and presidents is impossible), and Indian skepticism (Nagarjuna's circle that means of knowledge cannot be established without things known, illustrated with Stephen Sr. and Stephen Jr. as both father and son, plus Jayarasi's destruction of epistemology). He adds 'political skepticism' - the American sense that political knowledge is impossible - which breeds wikiality, an internet relativism ('reality we just agreed on') that the WØRD's own bullet points ('Wikipedia can tell a lie') undermine. Truthiness, he concludes, is Stephen's false cure for political skepticism: commitment without facts, a 'truthiness of the appearances'; but Sextus shows skeptics can still act on appearances without dogmatism, so we can vote and argue on the best evidence, as in Sagan's science-as-democracy, without certainty.

samples.book: 152 - The Ultimate Daily Show and Philosophy - More Moments of Zen, More Indecision Theory
samples.title: The Ultimate Daily Show and Philosophy
samples.relation: Barad maps fifth-century Athens onto contemporary America to cast Stewart as a Socratic reformer confronting modern sophists, advertisers, pundits and media figures who make weaker arguments appear stronger without caring about truth, exemplified by Ed Helms admitting network stories are pre-written from 'conventional wisdom' and Ann Coulter's conformity-peddling. She details the shared method: flattering the 'expert', feigned ignorance, and layer-by-layer questioning that traps targets like Rumsfeld ('It may not seem like much, but for this administration it's a huge policy shift') in contradiction, with Socratic irony doing the work of Stewart's awestruck deadpan and mute astonished reactions to Bush clips. Against Bill O'Reilly's 'stoned slacker' charge she cites the Annenberg finding that the show's young audience is better informed, and weighs Ken Tucker's 'monkey' question through the Crossfire 'I'm not going to be your monkey' exchange, concluding that, like Socrates facing trial and execution, Stewart uses irony as means and truth as end.

samples.book: 024 - Bullshit and Philosophy - Guaranteed to Get Perfect Results Every Time
samples.title: Bullshit as a Call to Open-Mindedness
samples.relation: Steve Fuller opens by asking whether bullshit detection coarsens the detector: Nietzsche and H.L. Mencken embraced the debunker's role (Mencken coining 'bunk'), while Ibsen's The Wild Duck and Hedda Gabler dramatize the need for a 'life lie', and detectors who find bullshit everywhere slide from nihilism into dogmatism. He re-reads bullshit as sophistry — the Sophists taught that securing your audience's belief is the only knowledge you need, against Socrates's attack and Plato's coining of 'rhetoric' to demonize them — and faults Frankfurt for calling the bullshitter 'indifferent' to truth when the accomplished bullshitter must be a keen student of what people tend to regard as true. The Sokal affair and Benjamin Franklin's 'economical with the truth' lead to his Kantian mapping of bullshitters (rationalists selecting among already-imaginable alternatives) against bullshit detectors (empiricists demanding evidence), which the scientific method will dialectically synthesize.

samples.book: 118 - Scott Adams and Philosophy - A Hole in the Fabric of Reality
samples.title: 1. How I Learned to Stop Worrying and Tolerate the Master Persuader Hypothesis
samples.relation: Wolfe reads Adams's Master Persuader hypothesis through the ancient quarrel between Socrates and the Sophists: Derren Brown's deflation of hypnosis into one personality dominating another leads to Gorgias's Encomium of Helen, where persuasive words are magic spells that steal free will, and to Plato's Gorgias, where Socrates condemns rhetoric as cookery and cosmetics that flatter the ignorant while his disciple Polus covets its tyrannical power. On this mapping Trump's plain-talk style is simply Aristotle's available means of persuasion for a particular audience, and Adams is mostly a Sophist who treats words as programming code for moist robots, though he keeps a Socratic sliver in his stated aim of exposing readers to different ideas rather than converting them. Wolfe closes by refusing both readings of Adams as pro-Trump troll or alt-right hero, urging each side to see how persuasion actually worked on them.

samples.book: 303 - Philosophy and the Interpretation of Pop Culture
samples.title: NOTES
samples.relation: Matthews argues that certain children's books are 'subversive' in a Socratic sense: they problematize concepts adults assume they command, challenging adult epistemic authority the way Socrates exposed the pretended knowledge of Athens' elite. Morris the Moose raises Aristotelian questions of natural kinds and essence-versus-accident; Leese Webster probes the concept of art; The Shrinking of Treehorn destabilizes 'normal' child development; Frog and Toad's 'The Garden' dramatizes the post hoc, ergo propter hoc fallacy about causation. In the Ozma of Oz Tik-Tok discussion, nine-year-old Paul reconstructs an argument that only brains think, which Matthews aligns with Searle's claim in The Mystery of Consciousness that consciousness is caused by specific neurobiological processes; he explicitly distinguishes his subversive stories from those promoting Pyrrhonian skepticism or Protagorean relativism.

samples.book: 253 - Asimov's Foundation and Philosophy - Psychohistory and Its Discontents
samples.title: 20. The Mystery of Math
samples.relation: Barta and Lee cast the debate over whether math is invented or discovered as Protagoras versus Pythagoras, mapped onto Foundation. Protagorean relativism ('man is the measure') and modern formalism (Hilbert, Poincaré) appear in the Empire's politicized, self-serving use of math and Gaal Dornick's culturally contingent base-ten counting, while Plato and Aristotle rebut relativism via the Theaetetus and the Law of Non-Contradiction ('if Hari's a liar, he dies'). Pythagorean realism/mathematical Platonism—numbers as the fundamental reality—appears in Luminism's holy number three, Kalle's poetic proofs, and the Foundationists' quasi-religious faith that psychohistory reveals reality's mathematical structure, with Gödel, Quine-Putnam indispensability, and Wigner's 'unreasonable effectiveness' as modern heirs and Aristotle as the standing critic.

samples.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
samples.title: 78. The Witness as Philosophy How Knowledge Is Constructed
samples.relation: Cuddy asks what epistemology Blow built into The Witness's frustrating puzzles and its windmill videos (Burke, Feynman, Moriarty, Spira, Gangaji). He rejects the sophistic/Protagorean 'knowledge depends on the observer' reading (most puzzles have objective, inductive-and-deductive solutions, e.g. the yellow-glass bunker) and the strict scientific realism of the Burke video defended by Putnam's no-miracles argument. Using Plato's cave and the aporia of Socrates' Meno (the puzzle's 'ah-ha' epiphanies), and Kuhn's incommensurable paradigm shifts (the game's 'hard left turns' forcing players to overhaul their understanding), he concludes the game argues that true knowledge is attainable, individually and collectively, though reached by a nonlinear, paradigm-shifting route rather than pure realism or relativism.

samples.book: 017 - Bob Dylan and Philosophy - It's Alright Ma (I'm Only Thinking)
samples.title: The Blessings of Tranquility
samples.relation: Michael Chiariello takes Dylan's "the truth is true whether you wanna believe it or not" as a correspondence theory of truth, then rejects both the gospel-era absolutism of "Precious Angel" and the relativism (from Protagoras' man-the-measure to modern subjectivism) that would make Dylan's changes of course harmless. The alternative he defends is Pyrrhonian skepticism in Sextus Empiricus's sense: truth is objective but never fully assured, so suspending judgment yields tranquility. Dylan's career - from the ambiguous "Blowin' in the Wind" through "Watching the River Flow" and "Things Have Changed" to the two versions of "Every Grain of Sand" ("the reality of man" vs "a perfect finished plan") - embodies this balanced, non-dogmatic search the way of God designed it.

samples.book: 049 - Zombies, Vampires, and Philosophy - New Life for the Undead
samples.title: Possibilities for Human-Vampire Co-operation
samples.relation: Douglas Glen Whitman uses Buffy's vampire brothel (humans paying vampires to feed on willing victims, as Giles concedes) and Blade's mandatory blood bank as two models of human-vampire coexistence to stage the clash between libertarianism (Nozick, Lomasky, Schmidtz) and welfarism (Singer, Unger, G.A. Cohen). He runs vampire personhood through Nozick's criteria from Anarchy, State, and Utopia — sentience, self-consciousness, rationality, free will, moral personality, soul — and argues no standard includes humans while excluding vampires, applying Singer's equal-consideration-of-suffering principle across kinds of beings. He then extends Singer's obligation-to-aid reasoning (rescuing a drowning child vs. donating to UNICEF) to show welfarism would mandate forced blood transfers or 'blood stamps', and argues via Adam Smith's Poor Law settlement rules and modern welfare-based anti-immigration politics that the burden of supporting dependents breeds exclusion. Only the libertarian brothel model of voluntary exchange, he concludes, turns vampire-human relations into a positive-sum game in which humans would actually come to recognize vampires as persons.

samples.book: 160 - Fallout and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Shelter
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: Matthew Watts sorts Fallout's artificial beings into cyborgs, synths, and pure robots and tests each against a theory of the self: Locke's memory theory explains the Robobrain socialites of Vault 118 and Nick Valentine's implanted prewar past, Parfit's psychological continuity (identity as a matter of degree) makes the Old World Blues Think Tank a caricature of a self stretched too thin, and Putnam's machine-table functionalism with multiple realizability (the Red Menace holotape running on any hardware) undermines Covenant's SAFE test by making function, not substrate, the mark of a mind. DiMA's excision of his own guilty memory in Far Harbor shows identity as Evan Thompson's enactive process rather than stored recall, since pruning memories can maintain or improve the self-in-progress. For moral standing below full personhood, Nussbaum's capabilities approach fits Curie's flourishing (research, companionship, watching a sunset in a synth body) and Singer's sentience criterion fits Victor the Securitron's avoidance of harm, exposing 'substrate prejudice' as a robot analog of speciesism - down to ED-E's triumphant arrival on the West Coast.

samples.book: 079 - Frankenstein and Philosophy - The Shocking Truth
samples.title: Frankenstein and Philosophy
samples.relation: Littmann argues that stripped of religious scruple, Shelley's own supreme virtue - kindness, embodied in Victor's family, Elizabeth, Clerval, and the cottagers - actually supports creating artificial life: the monster is benevolent until mistreated, and superior corpse-people would be a race of geniuses rather than a threat we may preemptively suppress. The monster himself invents utilitarianism ('relative as they were, as I applied them, to pleasure and pain alone'), De Lacey nearly lives it by promising the stranger rehabilitation over punishment, but Victor's case against building a mate is exposed as speciesism - he tallies unborn humans' futures while ignoring the joys of unborn cadaver folk, though utilitarians were the first to speak for animal rights. Since intelligent otherness is humanity's only chance at non-human friendship and the risks of Prometheus's fire paid off, the chapter rewrites the modern Prometheus as a blessing and ends with a re-imagined creation scene where the monster says 'I love you' to a Victor who finally names him Nigel.

samples.book: 196 - Terminator and Philosophy - I'll Be Back, Therefore I Am
samples.title: NOTES
samples.relation: Wayne Yuen asks whether Sarah was wrong not to kill Miles Dyson, weighing Kant's categorical imperative against utilitarian interest-maximization: killing one innocent to save three billion looks decisive until the interests of self-aware Skynet and the empathetic, self-sacrificing T-101 are counted on the machine side of the ledger. The chapter argues personhood turns on intelligence, self-awareness, empathy, and moral reasoning rather than DNA, so Skynet — which struck only after humans tried to pull the plug — has as strong a self-defense claim as we do. Mill's sophisticated utilitarianism then rescues common sense: rights protect the security that satisfies our deepest interests, and since Sarah's foreknowledge is unreliable (Reese's 'We'd won' changes the calculus), she should do what typically maximizes interests — spare Dyson and certainly not kill John. The tempting detour — that Judgment Day might itself be the morally preferable event, maximizing machine interests — is shown to collapse once overlooked facts like Reese's line are restored.

samples.book: 054 - The Onion and Philosophy - Fake News Story True, Alleges Indignant Area Professor
samples.title: The Onion’s New Environmental Ethic
samples.relation: Matthew Altman reads Onion environmental satire as a staged escape from anthropocentrism: 'New, Delicious Species Discovered' and 'Beauty Of National Forest Enjoyed By Logger' expose that even appreciating nature is just valuing it for us, while the mascara-testing lab rabbit and 'Funny Monkey Tested On' make Singer's speciesism charge vivid against factory farming and animal experiments. He then widens the argument to a biocentric concern for species and ecosystems via 'Stuffed-Animal Biodiversity Rising' and 'Consumer-Product Diversity Now Exceeds Biodiversity,' and to ecofeminism via 'Raped Environment Led Polluters On,' where the forest as flirtatious woman links domination of nature to sexism and victim-blaming. Global stories like the Bush 'national air conditioner' piece show Western overconsumption displacing blame onto Third World overpopulation, and 'I'm Doing My Inconsequential Part' satirizes the self-satisfaction of green consumerism itself — leaving the measure of the Onion's philosophical importance as how dangerous it is.

samples.book: 022 - The Undead and Philosophy - Chicken Soup for the Soulless
samples.title: Possibilities for Human-Vampire Co-operation
samples.relation: Douglas Glen Whitman contrasts two pop-culture templates: Buffy's vampire brothel, where willing humans pay vampires for consensual bites (Giles calls the customers 'willing victims'), and Blade's implied government blood bank, where humans are forced to donate. Running Robert Nozick's personhood criteria (sentience, rationality, free will, moral agency, soul) against vampires, he argues no standard admits humans while excluding them, so staking vampires violates rights and, on Singer's suffering-equals-suffering logic, refusing consideration is a kind of speciesism. The welfarist side - Singer and Unger's principle that we must prevent bad at little cost, as in the drowning child - would mandate Blade-style forced blood transfers, but Whitman contends such coercion breeds the very xenophobia (Adam Smith's Poor Law settlement rules, anti-immigrant welfare politics) that blocks recognizing vampire personhood. Only a libertarian market of voluntary exchange turns human-vampire relations from a zero-sum war into a positive-sum commerce.

samples.book: 122 - Westworld and Philosophy - Mind Equals Blown
samples.title: Whatever! It’s All Natural
samples.relation: Jaquet and Cova take the show's 'livestock' comparisons seriously and use animal ethics to test every justification for the guests' treatment of hosts. Direct speciesism (Logan: 'She's a goddamn doll') and indexical speciesism (Maeve's 'us versus them' to Bernard) both fail because mere species membership is morally irrelevant, like race or sex. The supposed human-exclusive markers also fail: hosts match us in intelligence (Maeve outclasses Stubbs), moral sense (Bernard's guilt over Theresa, Teddy's remorse over the massacre), and compatibilist free will - acts flowing from the agent's own desires - against Ford's determinism and Lutz's 'you don't have a choice.' They then refute the argument from nature (Ford's 'we murdered and butchered anything that challenged our primacy'), the Kantian person/tool contrast in the hosts' favor, Locke's creator-ownership ('I built your mind, Bernard'), and the 'better to exist' defense, concluding that because the hosts are conscious, they belong to the moral community alongside humans and animals.

samples.book: 074 - Planet of the Apes and Philosophy - Great Apes Think Alike
samples.title: Planet of the Apes and Philosophy
samples.relation: Travis Timmerman argues the series dramatizes Singer's equal consideration of interests: Zira frees Taylor once he writes 'My name is Taylor' because like interests must count equally regardless of species, while Dr. Zaius's erasing the writing, lobotomizing Landon, and destroying the cave artifacts is pure speciesism in Bentham's 'Can they suffer?' sense. He rejects the crude 'humans are smarter' argument (it would strip severely cognitively disabled humans of standing) and Nussbaum's species-normal version (it would permit caging Zira and Cornelius since normal apes are mute), then deploys Plato's Euthyphro dilemma against Locke-style God-given rights: a deity bellowing that human interests outrank ape interests is arbitrary unless grounded in independent reasons. Since farming severely cognitively disabled humans is obviously wrong and species membership is morally irrelevant, it is equally wrong to factory-farm and experiment on animals - so, like Caesar in Battle for the Planet of the Apes, become vegetarian.

samples.book: 155 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - The Truth Is Neither Here Nor There
samples.title: 6. Keeping It under Control
samples.relation: Mills reads Mr. Bates, the lame, twice-imprisoned, uncomplaining valet, as Downton's Epictetus, using him and the household to teach the Stoic dichotomy of control: only our judgments, desires, and actions are up to us, while jobs, reputations, and inheritances (Thomas's coveted valet post, Mary's scandal, Molesley's flower cup) are 'preferred indifferents' to be pursued without enslavement. Death figures as the great rejected indifferent, handled through Pamuk's demise and Mrs. Hughes's calm 'One day, I will die' upon finding a lump, as well as the grief of Isobel and Mary over Matthew. The closing section turns to Hierocles's concentric circles, with Sybil helping Gwen and Carson comforting Mary as drawing outsiders into the inner circle, a Stoic cosmopolitanism that Thomas, who sees the Crawleys as mere employers, fails entirely. The Dowager's 'I hope we're in control of something, if only ourselves' serves as the chapter's Stoic motto.

samples.book: 091 - It's Always Sunny and Philosophy - The Gang Gets Analyzed
samples.title: It’s Always Sunny and Philosophy
samples.relation: Greg Littmann systematically compares the Gang's values - wealth, attention, bad-assery ('Project Badass'), sexual conquest, relentless competition, revenge, pride in cheating, and callousness toward even friends and family - with the values Homer's Iliad and Odyssey celebrate, showing Achilles and Odysseus behave like the Gang: sacking cities, taking women as war trophies like Briseis, boasting of deception (the Trojan Horse), and rigging the funeral games.
