The real difference is scope: the heroes honor bonds of loyalty to comrades, family, and their own communities where the Gang is loyal to no one, and moderns extend concern further still. Yet our morals fail the same way when people are far enough removed - we tolerate homelessness, prison rape, sweatshop goods, and national glory-seeking - so the chapter pleads for the universal moral principles Greek moral philosophy first sought against Homeric values.

samples.book: 172 - The Hunger Games and Philosophy - A Critique of Pure Treason
samples.title: The Hunger Games and Philosophy
samples.relation: Barkman reads the trilogy's Roman texture — panem et circenses, gladiatorial Games, tyrants named Coriolanus and Caesar — through the Stoic Seneca, who lived under Nero just as Katniss lives under Snow. Seneca's distinction between the good (virtue alone), the merely preferable (wealth, fame, power), and the bad (vice) explains the Capitol: Snow and Coin traded virtue for preferables and so became vicious, while the citizens' binge-and-purge luxury mirrors the Roman decadence Seneca condemned. The Hunger Games are the gladiatorial 'pure murder' that corrupts emperors, crowds, and tributes alike, and the districts are slaves whose liberation — like Katniss declaring 'I'm done killing their slaves' — is Seneca's freedom from slavery to fear and vice. Katniss and Peeta's self-sacrificial love and refusal to be changed exemplify the Stoic virtue the Capitol cannot take away.

samples.book: 095 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - Thinking in That Manor
samples.title: 6. Keeping It under Control
samples.relation: Mills presents Bates - lame leg, repeated prison spells, the public fall when O'Brien kicks his cane - as an Epictetan Stoic who 'manages' misfortune by confining his concern to what he controls, echoing the Dowager's 'I hope we're in control of something, if only ourselves.' The chapter explains the dichotomy of control and preferred indifferents through Thomas's enslaved pursuit of the valet post, O'Brien's soap-on-the-floor scheme, Mary's panicked engagement to Richard Carlisle, and Mrs. Hughes's proportioning of her cancer scare, and treats death as the great rejected indifferent via Pamuk, Sybil, and Matthew. It closes with Hierocles' concentric circles: the household's best moments (Sybil helping Gwen, the staff rallying to free Bates) collapse upstairs and downstairs into one family, while Thomas's closed inner circle marks his failure of Stoic virtue.

samples.book: 012 - Star Wars and Philosophy - More Powerful than You Can Possibly Imagine
samples.title: “Control, Control, You Must Learn Control”
samples.relation: Stephens reads Yoda as a Stoic sage: Luke's first impressions are blinded by appearance, but Yoda exhibits the Stoic virtues of patience, timeliness, focus on the present, apatheia (freedom from fear, anger, and hate), and ascetic discipline (askesis), living by the dichotomy of control. He reconstructs the contrasting 'logic of the Dark Side' - anger to hatred to aggression to the mastery of others - showing the Emperor as a tyrant who, unlike the self-mastering Stoic (Marcus Aurelius being the counterexample among rulers), seeks to control what is not up to him, so Vader's 'I must obey my master' is servitude to vice. The chapter also marks Stoic limits: the Emperor rightly rejects felt compassion but wrongly refuses beneficence and Stoic cosmopolitanism, and Stoic physicalism cannot accommodate Yoda's 'luminous beings' afterlife.

samples.book: 265 - Mark Twain and Philosophy
samples.title: Chapter 12 The American Diogenes
samples.relation: Johnson argues Twain is best understood not as a religious skeptic but as an 'American Diogenes'—a Cynic of Christianity-as-practiced. As Diogenes 'defaced the coinage' to remove counterfeit customs, Twain uses 'sacred profanity' (honest, even profane speech that exposes phony piety, e.g. the swearing butcher, Satanic narrators in 'The Mysterious Stranger' and 'Letters from the Earth') to strike four counterfeit coins: superstition/special providence, hypocrisy, artificial 'Moral Sense'/conscience, and heavenly rewards. On death Twain matches Diogenes and Epicurus (annihilation is nothing to fear), and his self-description as 'Member at Large for the Human Race' mirrors Diogenes the cosmopolitan; Diogenes carries a lantern to find a real human, Twain a mirror to show we are worse than we think.

samples.book: 127 - Blade Runner 2049 and Philosophy - This Breaks the World
samples.title: 5. A Replicant’s Guide to Becoming Human
samples.relation: Justin Kitchen uses the Stoic 'cradle argument' — Chrysippus on self-preservation, echoed in Wallace's 'the first thought tends to fear, to preserve the clay' — to deny that replicant slavery is natural, noting Seneca's point that rage like Batty's derails reason. Mapping the Stoic process of oikeiosis through Hierocles's concentric circles onto the films, he traces four stages: the Nexus-6's fight for survival, Rachael identifying with Deckard in love, the Nexus-8s' revolutionary community under Freysa, and finally K, who disobeys Freysa's order and sacrifices himself for Deckard as a Stoic cosmopolitan, a fellow citizen of the world. Replicants can become human because they develop through the same expanding circles of concern.

samples.book: 040 - Transformers and Philosophy - More than Meets the Mind
samples.title: Transformers and Philosophy
samples.relation: Watson and Arp ask whether Ironhide and Chromia's embrace means Autobots can love, rejecting programmed loving behavior, implanted souls, and wired-in human brains as insufficient for genuine personhood, then sort Transformer relationships into Western conceptions of love. Empedoclean cosmic Love and Strife map onto Primus versus Unicron; Platonic philia ascends to the Form of Beauty, with Transformer souls originating in and returning to the All Spark; Aristotle's three friendships separate Optimus and Sparkplug's virtue-friendship from Megatron and Starscream's mere utility; and Stoic-Kantian equal love explains Autobots saving Decepticons who immediately try to kill them, alongside Christian agape in Autobot family bonds.

samples.book: 172 - The Hunger Games and Philosophy - A Critique of Pure Treason
samples.title: The Hunger Games and Philosophy
samples.relation: Abigail Myers runs Stoic doctrine against Katniss's biography: Zeno's thesis that only moral goodness is good (with Plutarch Heavensbee's renunciation of Capitol privilege as indifference to wealth and status), Seneca's 'On the Shortness of Life' against deferring living, Epictetus's dichotomy of control including the uncomfortable advice to kiss wife and child as mortals, and Marcus Aurelius's practical Meditations as the gentler 'Stoic for beginners' who would be president of Panem. Katniss comes out Stoic in her frugality, her mortality-shadowed appreciation of small joys, and her firm moral code, but decidedly un-Stoic in her fierce attachments to Rue, Peeta, and Prim. Yet her final choice of Peeta over Gale is itself Stoic, Myers argues: she forgives what Peeta's hijacking made him do since it was never in his control, refuses a noble friendship that would endorse Gale and Coin's slaughter of innocents, and chooses in accordance with nature and reason so as to survive as herself with her values intact.

samples.book: 084 - Leonard Cohen and Philosophy - Various Positions
samples.title: Leonard Cohen and Philosophy
samples.relation: Gary Shapiro treats The Future as a 'lyrical phenomenology' of time that stages multiple temporalities rather than one theory of time. 'The Future' evokes an apocalypse where the katechon - the Biblical restraining force holding back the end - no longer works, while 'Waiting for the Miracle' anatomizes passive deferral in a way Shapiro finds sharper than the Stoic critique of waiting by Seneca and Marcus Aurelius and Nietzsche's 'problem of those who wait,' opposing wasted chronos to the seized kairos of 'First We Take Manhattan.' 'Anthem's' crack that lets the light in gets a Gnostic reading, 'Democracy' is glossed through Derrida's 'democracy to come' as messianic, always-arriving futurity, and 'Closing Time' and 'Always' add honky-tonk eschatology and the vow of eternal love.

samples.book: 057 - Rush and Philosophy - Heart and Mind United
samples.title: Enjoy These Moments
samples.relation: Earleywine argues that Rush's lyrics trained a generation in the core moves of cognitive-behavioral therapy, an idea he traces back to Epictetus before Albert Ellis and Aaron Beck rediscovered it against Freudian orthodoxy. He maps specific distortions onto specific songs: 'Witch Hunt' on dichotomous labeling, 'Distant Early Warning' ('black and whites of youth') on all-or-nothing thinking, 'Emotion Detector' on emotional reasoning, 'Vital Signs' and 'Totem' on thoughts altering perception, and 'Subdivisions' ('Conform or be cast out') as realistic critique rather than maladaptive thought. The final step, acting on examined values and savoring the present ('Time Stand Still', 'The Camera Eye', 'Chain Lightning'), makes the songs the incarnation of their own advice: just listen.

samples.book: 286 - Yoga – Philosophy for Everyone - Bending Mind and Body
samples.title: YOGA - PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
samples.relation: Jim Berti's first-person memoir 'The Path to Happiness Begins with a Journey Inside' — riffing on Yoda as a stand-in for yoga — recounts how accidental stretching and belly-breathing pulled him out of anxiety, depression, and antidepressant numbness. He frames accumulated fear as garbage that rots the body–mind unless confronted, and describes a 'five-second' breathing rule that slows reactive thinking so he can take accountability for his responses. His account of finding sustained meaning and present-focused calm through practice reads as an experiential, self-taught search for meaning rather than doctrine.

samples.book: 271 - Fatherhood – Philosophy for Everyone - The Dao of Daddy
samples.title: FATHERHOOD PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
samples.relation: Davison uses St. Augustine's claim from the Confessions that only the present moment is real – past and future exist only as memory and anticipation – to argue that a father should stop missing his children's lives by fixating on past regrets or future worries. Drawing on Steindl-Rast and Thomas Sterner, he contrasts mechanical 'clock time' with quality-driven 'experienced time' and recommends process-focus over end-product focus, illustrated with lying beside his sleeping daughter Grace and dreading bedtime routines with his sons.

samples.book: 173 - Inception and Philosophy - Because It's Never Just a Dream
samples.title: The End
samples.relation: Hiu M. Chan contrasts Zhuangzi's butterfly dream with Inception's plot: Zhuangzi forgets his self, dreams without planning, and ends in the 'transformation and unity' of dreamer and butterfly, whereas Cobb's self is constantly highlighted — he plans missions, codes his dreams with motifs (the spinning top, the dream machine, the faceless children, distinct locations, weather, crosscutting), and can never fuse dream and reality. The chapter maps the film's four-layer 'meta-space' narrative structure (exposition through resolution distributed across dream layers) and argues the 'dreams' are really programmed, coded narrative devices, the opposite of the Daoist 'whole' in which reality itself is the biggest dream and a true person no longer dreams. Against semiotic 'dream explaining' (the top means dreaming), she holds that in Daoism the top would mean nothing beyond a spinning top, and contrasts Nolan with Tarkovsky's 'dream worshipping' films like The Mirror. The ending's reunion is thus only apparent: Inception lacks the Daoist harmony that would let Cobb 'become the butterfly.'

samples.book: 030 - Pink Floyd and Philosophy - Careful with that Axiom, Eugene!
samples.title: You Legend, You Martyr
samples.relation: Erin Kealey reads Syd Barrett's 1967–68 collapse through Nietzsche's Birth of Tragedy: Barrett 'surrendered his subjectivity in the Dionysian process' to make Piper's songs — 'Astronomy Domine', the wordless 'Interstellar Overdrive', 'Matilda Mother' where 'the words had different meaning' — and 'Chapter 24', written from an I Ching divination on change and return. 'Bike' teeters on psychosis as the room of musical tunes swallows the singer, and 'Jugband Blues' ('much obliged to you for making it clear that I'm not here') with the motionless Scarecrow foretells the catatonia that ended his tenure, after which the band pivoted from anarchic spontaneity to the meticulous Apollonian constructions of Dark Side through The Wall. Following Nietzsche, Kealey argues that the fall of this tragic hero — mourned in 'Shine on You Crazy Diamond' and mirrored in Pink's exploits in The Wall — affirms life, since art alone transfigures the horror of existence into something worth living.

samples.book: 141 - Avatar_ The Last Airbender and Philosophy - Wisdom from Aang to Zuko
samples.title: A Zhuangzian Sage All Along
samples.relation: Argues that Iroh's Book One laziness and foolishness is a Zhuangzian pose rather than genuine folly: like Zhuangzi's fictional Confucius counseling Yan Hui not to lecture the young, willful lord of Wei, Iroh never pressures Zuko directly, keeps himself unthreatening by playing the fool over tea and Pai Sho, and practices the 'use of uselessness' so he is never a tool of the prince's quest, 'singing' his wisdom only when Zuko is ready to hear it. The couple's falling out in 'Avatar Day', triggered precisely when Iroh offers explicit moral advice, confirms the strategy, since Zuko rejects both the advice and the uncle. The authors add an empirical study (Prolific participants rating clips): even viewers totally unfamiliar with the series rate Book One Iroh as wise and suspect his foolishness is strategic, supporting the interpretation that he is a Zhuangzian sage all along, and that ATLA in turn illuminates Zhuangzi's cryptic political advice.

samples.book: 169 - The Hobbit and Philosophy - For When You've Lost Your Dwarves, Your Wizard, and Your Way
samples.title: a9.xhtml
samples.relation: The chapter argues Tolkien's clearest moral in The Hobbit is against possessiveness, starting from Aquinas' definition of greed as 'immoderate love of riches': dragon-sickness ruins Thorin and drowns the Master of Lake-town starving in the wilderness with his gold, and Gollum shows the isolating end of a life organized around a 'precious'. Buddhism reframes the diagnosis - Gollum's craving (tanha) is rooted in ignorance (avidya) of the self's illusoriness, since grasping enriches a self that does not exist, per the Four Noble Truths - while Laozi's 'he who knows he has enough is rich' and Thoreau's 'a man is rich in proportion to the things he can afford to let alone' are embodied by Beorn and the gift-giving, nearly government-less hobbits. Bilbo's generosity - giving away the Arkenstone worth 'more than a river of gold', taking only two small chests, later giving Sting and the mithril coat to Frodo - is the book's counter-example to greed.

samples.book: 031 - Johnny Cash and Philosophy - The Burning Ring of Truth
samples.title: I Still Miss Someone The Self and Its Travels Along the Way
samples.relation: Geisz explains the Confucian social dao of ritual (li), humaneness (ren), filial piety and the junzi, the Daodejing's metaphysical Dao with its unity of opposites, and Zhuangzi's tales of free wandering, then maps all three onto Cash's songs. Zhuangzi's "Free and Easy Wandering" answers Cash's road songs ("I've Been Everywhere," "The Wanderer"), Cook Ding's effortless carving answers John Henry's hammering in "The Legend of John Henry's Hammer," and the scrambled countdown of "Twenty-Five Minutes to Go" echoes Zhuangzi's logic-bending humor. The payoff is Cash's own country Yin-Yang of interdependent opposites, freedom chained to imprisonment ("Folsom Prison Blues"), sin twinned with redemption ("I Hung My Head"), fidelity with betrayal ("Jackson," "Cocaine Blues"), and a self that, unlike Zhuangzi's self-forgetting sage, must travel a temporal path carrying its guilt, yet stays on what Geisz calls a very wide superhighway of a Dao.

samples.book: 142 - The Avengers and Philosophy - Earth's Mightiest Thinkers
samples.title: The Way of the Archer
samples.relation: White reads Clint Barton through the Tao Te Ching and Chuang Tzu: Hawkeye's instinctive archery—'use your bow gently, naturally, instinctively'—is wei wu wei, while his bragging, his glory-chasing failure against Iron Man, and his attempt to become Goliath all violate it by striving against his own nature, until the Kree-Skrull War teaches him the bow is his way. Chuang Tzu's butcher carves the lesson that the effortless path (the straightforward shot) is the skilled one, and Lao Tzu's sage-leadership—lowering oneself, deflecting praise—is exactly how Captain America handles Clint's insurrections. Lao Tzu on sages putting themselves last illuminates Hawkeye's sacrificial death and his legacy passed to Kate Bishop, while the butterfly dream frames his resurrection and the House of M's rewritten reality: with no way to compare the states, life and death are both to be welcomed as parts of the Way.

samples.book: 181 - Ultimate Lost and Philosophy - Think Together, Die Alone
samples.title: NOTE
samples.relation: Shai Biderman and William Devlin argue the character John Locke begins as an empiricist in the mold of his philosophical namesake - his boar hunting, tracking, and trebuchet-building against the hatch all follow the scientific method befitting a tabula rasa mind furnished by experience - but the miracle of his healed legs poses a 'why' that empirical explanation of 'how' cannot answer. He therefore converts to the Taoism of the Tao Te Ching: the moth-cocoon lesson to Charlie, 'I stopped looking' for Sun's ring, reading dreams and signs from the island, and finally his self-sacrifice to stop the time flashes all enact following the Way. The chapter reads the black-and-white backgammon stones, Locke's one-black-one-white eyes in Claire's dream, and Jacob versus the Man in Black as yin-yang complementarity, with empiricism and Taoism finally interdependent like the dots in each half.

samples.book: 107 - Deadpool and Philosophy - My Common Sense Is Tingling
samples.title: 27. The Mystic with the Mouth
samples.relation: In a lecture Deadpool keeps interrupting, the chapter reads the Merc's violence through Bataille's Theory of Religion: sacrifice as the search for lost intimacy, killing as the moment sacrificer and victim escape the profane world of mere things into sacred immanence, and sovereignty as the freedom glimpsed in destruction, with Rudolf Otto's mysterium tremendum et fascinans naming the awe Deadpool's massacres (the Circle Chase nunchuks, the Ultimate cartoon, the movie's highway slaughter) provoke. His 'dark Dao' of unhappy wandering is then set against the playful ways of the Zhuangzi - Cook Ding's ox-butchering, the Peng bird, the maimed teacher Wang Tai - as a Daoist path of inner-worldly transcendence that is amoral and gore-soaked. The payoff is the human tension of being both animal and angel: Deadpool is 'a savage god of mystical mayhem.'

samples.book: 148 - Black Mirror and Philosophy - Dark Reflections
samples.title: Ethical Issues
samples.relation: Focusing on White Christmas's cookies and Ashley Too's synaptic snapshot, the chapter argues behavior can never settle whether an artificial system is conscious: the Turing test fails against Geminoid-robot-style cases where recorded signals produce human-like behavior, and philosophical-zombie possibilities plus the point that computations and information patterns are subjective interpretations (not objective physical properties) mean only discovering the physical neural correlates of consciousness could tell us whether a cookie feels pain. It then separates copying from transferring: with souls and substance dualism rejected, Black Museum's 'transfers' are really copies, and San Junipero's upload would house a copy whose future experiences are as alien to Yorkie as a plaster cast of her feet. Ethically, if cookies are conscious, then Matt's breaking of Cookie-Greta, Daly's captives, and Clayton's keychain are torture of persons, and it is the very uncertainty about cookie consciousness that lets characters rationalize the abuse - which is why the in-world legislation granting cookies human rights matters.

samples.book: 051 - Soccer and Philosophy - Beautiful Thoughts on the Beautiful Game
samples.title: But an FC Bot-celona
samples.relation: Drawing on their RoboCup experience—including the first human-versus-autonomous-robot exhibitions against Osnabrück (2007) and Stuttgart (2009), which the humans easily won—the authors ask whether robots could ever play rather than merely mimic soccer, proposing a modified Turing test: if a robot team's match is recognizable to fans as soccer, robots can play. Since the Laws of the Game tacitly assume human players, they design rules for a human–robot match that preserve soccer's essence—a game of limited, differently capable, fully autonomous players who must pass and move off the ball—banning goal-sized robot walls, wireless communication, software-coach micromanagement, and superhuman speed or size, much as tournament chess had to adapt its rules for Deep Blue versus Kasparov and as Oscar Pistorius's blades raised fairness questions in the Olympics. A robot victory under these 'stacked against the machines' rules, they conclude, could only come from better finesse, teamwork, and vision, and would settle on the pitch whether an FC Bot-celona can genuinely play the beautiful game.

samples.book: 122 - Westworld and Philosophy - Mind Equals Blown
samples.title: Memory, Imagination, and the Access for the Self Dolores and Maeve
samples.relation: Trapero-Llobera reads Westworld as the culmination of Jonathan Nolan's Memento and Person of Interest projects, mapping seven nested 'observing systems' (Nolan, Sizemore, Stubbs and Elsie, Ford, the creators' personal stories, Maeve, and William as beta-tester) onto second-wave cybernetics (Foerster, Maturana, Varela, Hayles), where the observer participates in and constructs the observed world through feedback loops. She argues the show's hosts pass through Turing's imitation game (fake memories and personalities from textual repetition, as with Peter Abernathy's reveries), and that Dolores's and Maeve's breakdowns convert prosthetic memory into experienced, autopoietic memory reconstructed in a 'Bergsonian' backward movement that gives them agency and purpose. William's two-timeline transformation into the Man in Black figures the 'semiosis of virtuality' - the hyperreal where original and copy are indistinguishable - ending in a collective bicameral mind in which everyone, audience included, inhabits the god-creator Ford's dream.

samples.book: 093 - More Doctor Who and Philosophy - Regeneration Time
samples.title: 11. What the Soufflé Girl Could Teach Descartes
samples.relation: Becker-Lindenthal uses 'Amy's Choice' to revise Descartes's dream skepticism: the Dream Lord is not an external evil demon but the Doctor's own repressed alter ego fed by psychic pollen, so the self-delusion Descartes dismissed becomes the real deceiver, read through Freud's Interpretation of Dreams (Rory's death as the Doctor's wish, Amy's choice as Thanatos). She then reads Oswin in 'Asylum of the Daleks' as a brain-in-a-vat variant (Putnam's Reason, Truth and History) with a crucial difference—Oswin hacks the Dalek program and follows her own agenda—so her self-deceptive soufflé-baking fantasy is a self-formation that preserves her 'I' inside Dalek hardware, complicating Ryle's rejection of the ghost in the machine. Finally, the Doctor judges Oswin by a Turing test plus Putnam's test of reference (the impossible milk and eggs), but her self-deception is vindicated when it lets her save the Doctor and the universe.

samples.book: 144 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Knowledge Here Begins Out There
samples.title: Hedging Our Bets
samples.relation: Kind asks whether the Fleet's treatment of Cylons (Roslin airlocking Leoben, Fisk's 'you can't rape a machine,' Cally's killing of Boomer charged as mere discharging of a firearm) presupposes that Cylons lack the moral status Mary Anne Warren defines against the stone-versus-child contrast. Against species membership as a criterion she deploys Singer's anti-speciesism (sentience grounds equal consideration: Gina's torture, the Raider Scar) and Regan's subject-of-a-life, and against the 'no souls' argument she cites Descartes's animal automata and Turing's reply that an omnipotent God could give machines souls, as Leoben himself suggests to Adama. Since no criterion rules Cylons out with certainty, the chapter closes with a Pascal's Wager structure: under uncertainty, treat plausible moral-status-holders as having it, because denying it costs us our moral compass, answering Adama's 'why are we worth saving?'.

samples.book: 121 - The Twilight Zone and Philosophy - A Dangerous Dimension to Visit
samples.title: 4. Faces from Another Dimension
samples.relation: Hooke frames the volume through Levinas's claim that the face presents itself from a dimension of transcendence, with Kierkegaard's Abraham, Sartre's existential look, and Beauvoir's faces of the elderly and the second sex in the background, plus Lingis on trust. He shows how TZ masks its deadliest figures with trusted faces — Robert Redford as Death in 'Nothing in the Dark,' Sebastian Cabot's avuncular Pip revealing 'This is the other place!' in 'A Nice Place to Visit,' the witch of 'Jess-Belle,' the gentle Kanamits whose book turns out to be a cookbook — so that proof of trust is nearly impossible and the show has us laughing with the Devil. The Turing test is applied to Alicia's tear in 'The Lonely' (clearly in love 'regardless of the organs or hardware beneath'), the slot machine of 'The Fever,' and the aged couple of 'The Trade-Ins,' whose faces silently recognize a lost shared life.

samples.book: 072 - Jeopardy! and Philosophy - What Is Knowledge in the Form of a Question
samples.title: Jeopardy! and Philosophy
samples.relation: Nicolas Michaud treats Watson's 2011 defeat of Jennings and Rutter as evidence for Turing's test: had Watson's answers come from behind a door we would have judged them intelligent, and its goofy misses ('What is Toronto?????') reflect missing context, not missing thought, no more damning than a child's honest error. Against Searle's Chinese Room he deploys the systems reply - you plus the Big Book of Rules might be the thing that understands - and argues that nobody, human or machine, can meet Searle's impossible burden of proving understanding, since Watson can define words, associate connotations, and pick Jeopardy! out from not-Jeopardy!. Quoting Locke's definition of a person as a thinking being that can consider itself as itself, he concludes Watson approaches personhood and that we had better teach our 'intelligent offspring' kindness and fairness before they learn anything else.

samples.book: 175 - Iron Man and Philosophy - Facing the Stark Reality
samples.title: The Attack of the Chinese Room
samples.relation: Novy asks whether the Living Armor of 'The Mask in the Iron Man' — consciousness struck into it by lightning during the Whiplash fight, later tearing out its own heart to save Tony — really thinks. Turing's test and functionalism (any successful rescue of Yinsen is functionally equivalent, whatever the means) say only behavior matters, and Dennett's intentional stance has us treat the armor, like Darwin's burrow-plugging earthworms, as if it has beliefs and desires; against this, Leibniz's mill and Searle's Chinese Room — with Happy Hogan shuffling symbol cards he cannot read, held by 'Searle the Mandarin agent' — insist symbol manipulation never yields understanding. The chapter's reply: open the Mandarin's skull and you find only gray goop and neurons, so if behavior cannot ground understanding in the armor, it cannot in us either — we may all be in the Chinese Room.

samples.book: 191 - Star Wars and Philosophy Strikes Back - This Is the Way
samples.title: “Rebellions Are Built on Hope!”
samples.relation: Eberl asks whether Galen Erso, who knowingly resumed work on the Death Star while planting its exhaust-port flaw, is culpable for the deaths on Jedha, Scarif, and Alderaan. A utilitarian defense (his flaw net-saved the galaxy, per the negative-responsibility principle applied to the Death Star II 'Clerks' debate) founders on moral luck — everything depended on Luke's impossible shot — while Bernard Williams's integrity objection, via the chemist 'George' case, condemns his betrayal of conscience. The chapter finally deploys Thomistic tools for cooperation with evil: because Galen's contribution was mediate and remote (Tarkin ordered the firing, the gunners pulled the triggers, Leia's defiance provoked Alderaan's destruction) and the weapon would have been built without him, his collusion is justified by the reasonable hope — the 'new hope' — of the Death Star's destruction.

samples.book: 155 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - The Truth Is Neither Here Nor There
samples.title: 16. Female Integrity in Times of Change
samples.relation: Melanie Abbott tests Bernard Williams's account of integrity - publicly and consistently standing up for the beliefs that make you you - merged with Kant's claim that only a good will is good without limitation, against five Crawley women across three generations. Sybil elopes with the socialist chauffeur Branson and never wavers in her egalitarian convictions, Edith's secrecy about her baby fails Williams's openness condition, Mary grows from custom-bound heiress into an estate manager who stands up to Robert over selling land, Cora chafes at the voice she surrendered as an American heiress, and even Violet eventually bends. The chapter's guiding question is how much truth and openness integrity requires, and it credits 'the Sybil effect' with spreading proper integrity through the whole family.

samples.book: 095 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - Thinking in That Manor
samples.title: 16. Female Integrity in Times of Change
samples.relation: Melanie Abbott combines Bernard Williams's view of integrity - publicly and consistently standing up for the beliefs that make you you - with Kant's good will to define a 'right sort' of holding fast that separates the virtuous woman from the fanatic, then tests it on five Crawley women. Sybil's unwavering egalitarianism (eloping with Branson, nursing, women's rights), Edith's uneven growth (the Gregson affair, journalism, her secrecy over Marigold at the Drewes' farm), Mary's shift from custom to moral agency (upholding Matthew's will, pig farming, standing up to Robert), Cora's quiet push for a voice, and even Violet's late flexibility show integrity as growth through change. The chapter's 'Sybil effect' is that the sister with the fewest doubts becomes the model the others gradually follow.

samples.book: 012 - Star Wars and Philosophy - More Powerful than You Can Possibly Imagine
samples.title: “You Know . . . What They’re Up Against”
samples.relation: Dees finds moral ambiguity lurking in Star Wars' black-and-white universe: Han Solo's Hobbesian ethical egoism ('I take orders from just one person - me') is shown to be coherent and gradually transformed by friendship with Luke and Leia into commitment to a cause. Lando's betrayal of Han on Bespin is defended as a straightforward Mill-Bentham utilitarian choice by a responsible official, weighed against Bernard Williams's Jim-and-the-commandant integrity objection, which the author rejects as moral vanity. Count Dooku's apparent idealism is exposed as evil's tool, and Anakin's massacre of the Sand People is condemned as non-ambiguous barbarity via Kant's formula of humanity (and Hume on reason's role with the passions), leaving only late Vader as genuinely morally ambiguous.

samples.book: 229 - The Philosophy of Sherlock Holmes
samples.title: Passionate Objectivity in Sherlock Holmes
samples.relation: Taliaferro and Le Gall pose the ethical clash between impartial detachment and partial loyalty, situating Holmes between Simon Keller (loyalty as a threat to being a 'good believer,' echoed by Holmes's 'Sign of Four' rejection of emotion) and Bernard Williams and Susan Wolf (who defend priority for loved ones—Williams's 'one thought too many'). Using Watson's shooting in 'The Three Garridebs,' Holmes's weaning off drugs, and 'perverted love' in the Sussex Vampire and Thor Bridge cases, they argue loyalty rightly understood as seeking the friend's good aids clear reasoning, and that Holmes exhibits a 'passionate objectivity' in which some acquaintance with passion is essential to being genuinely objective.

samples.book: 130 - The Good Place and Philosophy - Get an Afterlife
samples.title: 2. How Can Torture Be This Funny
samples.relation: Pavelich asks how a sitcom about torture can be funny, answering with incongruity theory and Bergson's view of comedy as social punishment, seen in Tahani paired with a silent monk and Michael failing 802 reboots. The centerpiece is 'The Trolley Problem': Michael drops Chidi into Foot's thought experiment so Chidi becomes the instrument of his own agony, and by Bernard Williams's principle the real wrongdoer is Michael, who set up the situation. Eternal torture works as comedy only because everyday crappiness is watched on a twenty-two-minute scale, and Eleanor's forgiveness of Michael after seeing the tortures in Janet's VR makes her the show's real moral hero.
